doi:10.1038/s41592-026-03272-x.abstract: Cell segmentation is a critical yet under-standardized step in spatial transcriptomics, directly affecting cell identity assignment, spatial organization and downstream biological interpretation. Despite rapid advances in spatial transcriptomics technologies, systematic evaluations of segmentation methods across platforms and biological contexts remain limited. Here we benchmark 11 image-based, transcriptomics-based and multimodal segmentation methods across 15 datasets generated by 5 spatial transcriptomics technologies, spanning 12 human and mouse tissue types. We introduce biologically informed evaluation metrics that quantify segmentation quality, transcript recovery, cell composition, morphology, expression purity and spatial organization. Benchmarking reveals substantial variation in performance across datasets, technologies and evaluation criteria, highlighting trade-offs among segmentation completeness, transcriptomic fidelity and biological interpretability. Cross-technology analyses further demonstrate that segmentation choice critically shapes downstream analyses, including cell-type specificity, transcript contamination and ligand-receptor inference. Together, our unified Nextflow pipeline provides a scalable foundation for standardized evaluation of segmentation and method selection in spatial transcriptomics.

doi:10.1038/s41592-026-03274-9.abstract: Biological systems exhibit complex hierarchical regulation, with interactions across multiple layers governing transitions between states. Identifying the causal architecture underlying these state transitions remains challenging because confounding can produce spurious associations in observational data. Here we present CauTrigger, a hierarchical deep latent variable model that integrates do-calculus to identify potential causal triggers and predict perturbation outcomes across multiple regulatory layers. By disentangling causal and spurious latent factors, CauTrigger recursively reconstructs the underlying regulatory hierarchy and enables interpretable reasoning from observational data. Across synthetic and real-world datasets with multilayer regulatory structures, CauTrigger outperforms existing methods in identifying causal triggers and forecasting system-level responses. Applied to single-cell multi-omics and gut microbiome datasets, CauTrigger prioritizes candidate causal triggers and uses in silico perturbations to generate testable hypotheses about biological state transitions and inform potential strategies for state navigation. Together, these results establish CauTrigger as a general-purpose framework for causal discovery in complex biological systems.

doi:10.1038/s41698-017-0023-0.abstract: Abstract Reduction-oxidation factor 1-apurinic/apyrimidinic endonuclease (Ref-1/APE1) is a critical node in tumor cells, both as a redox regulator of transcription factor activation and as part of the DNA damage response. As a redox signaling protein, Ref-1/APE1 enhances the transcriptional activity of STAT3, HIF-1α, nuclear factor kappa B, and other transcription factors to promote growth, migration, and survival in tumor cells as well as inflammation and angiogenesis in the tumor microenvironment. Ref-1/APE1 is activated in a variety of cancers, including prostate, colon, pancreatic, ovarian, lung and leukemias, leading to increased aggressiveness. Transcription factors downstream of Ref-1/APE1 are key contributors to many cancers, and Ref-1/APE1 redox signaling inhibition slows growth and progression in a number of tumor types. Ref-1/APE1 inhibition is also highly effective when paired with other drugs, including standard-of-care therapies and therapies targeting pathways affected by Ref-1/APE1 redox signaling. Additionally, Ref-1/APE1 plays a role in a variety of other indications, such as retinopathy, inflammation, and neuropathy. In this review, we discuss the functional consequences of activation of the Ref-1/APE1 node in cancer and other diseases, as well as potential therapies targeting Ref-1/APE1 and related pathways in relevant diseases. APX3330, a novel oral anticancer agent and the first drug to target Ref-1/APE1 for cancer is entering clinical trials and will be explored in various cancers and other diseases bringing bench discoveries to the clinic.

doi:10.1038/s41698-021-00211-1.abstract: Abstract Neuroendocrine prostate cancer is an aggressive variant of prostate cancer that may arise de novo or develop from pre-existing prostate adenocarcinoma as a mechanism of treatment resistance. The combined loss of tumor suppressors RB1, TP53, and PTEN are frequent in NEPC but also present in a subset of prostate adenocarcinomas. Most clinical and preclinical studies support a trans-differentiation process, whereby NEPC arises clonally from a prostate adenocarcinoma precursor during the course of treatment resistance. Here we highlight a case of NEPC with significant intra-patient heterogeneity observed across metastases. We further demonstrate how single-cell genomic analysis of circulating tumor cells combined with a phenotypic evaluation of cellular diversity can be considered as a window into tumor heterogeneity in patients with advanced prostate cancer.

doi:10.1038/s41698-023-00407-7.abstract: Abstract Cyclin dependent kinases (CDKs) are serine/threonine kinases that are proposed as promising candidate targets for cancer treatment. These proteins complexed with cyclins play a critical role in cell cycle progression. Most CDKs demonstrate substantially higher expression in cancer tissues compared with normal tissues and, according to the TCGA database, correlate with survival rate in multiple cancer types. Deregulation of CDK1 has been shown to be closely associated with tumorigenesis. CDK1 activation plays a critical role in a wide range of cancer types; and CDK1 phosphorylation of its many substrates greatly influences their function in tumorigenesis. Enrichment of CDK1 interacting proteins with Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) pathway analysis was conducted to demonstrate that the associated proteins participate in multiple oncogenic pathways. This abundance of evidence clearly supports CDK1 as a promising target for cancer therapy. A number of small molecules targeting CDK1 or multiple CDKs have been developed and evaluated in preclinical studies. Notably, some of these small molecules have also been subjected to human clinical trials. This review evaluates the mechanisms and implications of targeting CDK1 in tumorigenesis and cancer therapy.

doi:10.1038/s41698-023-00494-6.abstract: Abstract Accurate prognosis for cancer patients can provide critical information for optimizing treatment plans and improving life quality. Combining omics data and demographic/clinical information can offer a more comprehensive view of cancer prognosis than using omics or clinical data alone and can also reveal the underlying disease mechanisms at the molecular level. In this study, we developed and validated a deep learning framework to extract information from high-dimensional gene expression and miRNA expression data and conduct prognosis prediction for breast cancer and ovarian-cancer patients using multiple independent multi-omics datasets. Our model achieved significantly better prognosis prediction than the current machine learning and deep learning approaches in various settings. Moreover, an interpretation method was applied to tackle the “black-box” nature of deep neural networks and we identified features (i.e., genes, miRNA, demographic/clinical variables) that were important to distinguish predicted high- and low-risk patients. The significance of the identified features was partially supported by previous studies.

doi:10.1038/s41698-024-00564-3.abstract: Abstract In hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), classical cancer stem cells (CSC) markers were shared by normal stem cells, targeting which may hinder hepatic regeneration and cause liver failure. Additionally, the spatial structure of CSC still remained elusive. To address these limitations, we undertook a comprehensive study combining single-cell data (56,022 cells from 20 samples) and spatial data (38,191 spots from eight samples) to obtain CSC signature and uncover its spatial structure. Utilizing the CytoTRACE algorithm, we discretely identified CSC, which displayed upregulated proliferation pathways regulated by HIF1A. A CSC signature of 107 genes was then developed using Weighted Gene Co-expression Network Analysis (WGCNA). Notably, HCC patients with high CSC levels exhibited an accumulation of SPP1+ macrophages (Macro_SPP1) expressing metalloproteinases (MMP9, MMP12, and MMP7) regulated by HIF1A, suggesting a hypoxic tumor region connecting Macro_SPP1 and CSC. Both CSC and Macro_SPP1 correlated with worse prognosis and undesirable immunotherapy response. Spatial analysis revealed the co-location of CSC and Macro_SPP1, with CD8 T cells excluded from the tumor region. The co-location area and non-tumor area of boundary exhibited a high level of hypoxia, with the HAVRC2 checkpoint highly expressed. Within the co-location area, the SPP1 signaling pathway was most active in cell-cell communication, with SPP1-CD44 and SPP1-ITGA/ITGB identified as the main ligand-receptor pairs. This study successfully constructed a CSC signature and demonstrated the co-location of CSC and Macro_SPP1 in a hypoxic region that exacerbates the tumor microenvironment in HCC.

doi:10.1038/s41698-024-00630-w.abstract: Abstract Anti-PD(L)-1 inhibition combined with platinum doublet chemotherapy (Chemo-IO) has become the most frequently used standard of care regimen in patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). The negative impact of antibiotics on clinical outcomes prior to anti-PD(L)-1 inhibition monotherapy (IO) has been demonstrated in multiple studies, but the impact of antibiotic exposure prior to initiation of Chemo-IO is controversial. We assessed antibiotic exposures at two time windows: within 60 days prior to therapy (-60 d window) and within 60 days prior to therapy and 42 days after therapy (-60 + 42d window) in 2028 patients with advanced NSCLC treated with Chemo-IO and IO monotherapy focusing on objective response rate (ORR: rate of partial response and complete response), progression-free survival (PFS), and overall survival (OS). We also assessed impact of antibiotic exposure in an independent cohort of 53 patients. Univariable and multivariable analyses were conducted along with a meta-analysis from similar studies. For the -60 d window, in the Chemo-IO group ( N = 769), 183 (24%) patients received antibiotics. Antibiotic exposure was associated with worse ORR (27% vs 40%, p = 0.001), shorter PFS (3.9 months vs. 5.9 months, hazard ratio [HR] 1.35, 95%CI 1.1,1.6, p = 0.0012), as well as shorter OS (10 months vs. 15 months, HR 1.50, 95%CI 1.2,1.8, p = 0.00014). After adjusting for known prognostic factors in NSCLC, antibiotic exposure was independently associated with worse PFS (HR 1.39, 95%CI 1.35,1.7, p = 0.002) and OS (HR 1.61, 95%CI 1.28,2.03, p < 0.001). Similar results were obtained in the -60 + 42d window, and also in an independent cohort. In a meta-analysis of patients with NSCLC treated with Chemo-IO ( N = 4) or IO monotherapy ( N = 13 studies) antibiotic exposure before treatment was associated with worse OS among all patients ( n = 11,351) (HR 1.93, 95% CI 1.52, 2.45) and Chemo-IO-treated patients ( n = 1201) (HR 1.54, 95% CI 1.28, 1.84). Thus, antibiotics exposure prior to Chemo-IO is common and associated with worse outcomes, even after adjusting for other factors. These results highlight the need to implement antibiotic stewardship in routine oncology practice.

doi:10.1038/s41698-025-01011-7.abstract: Abstract Immune-checkpoint targeting Drug Conjugates (IDCs) are a novel class of therapeutics that combine an immune checkpoint-targeting moiety, a cleavable linker, and a cytotoxic payload. By integrating features and functions of antibody-drug conjugates and immunotherapy, IDCs represent a promising strategy to remodel the tumor microenvironment and enhance antitumor efficacy. Several IDCs targeting checkpoints such as PD-L1, B7-H3, and B7-H4 are in early-phase clinical trials. This review summarizes available data on IDC efficacy and toxicity in human. Although current evidence is limited, ongoing phase III trials and biomarker studies will clarify their optimal clinical role, including potential for tumor-agnostic use.

doi:10.1038/s41698-026-01622-8.abstract: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) are central orchestrators of immune evasion, therapeutic resistance, and clinical outcome across diverse solid tumors. However, the classical M1/M2 paradigm fails to capture the lineage diversity, spatial heterogeneity, and functional plasticity of TAMs within the tumor microenvironment. Unlike previous reviews that mainly summarize macrophage polarization or TAM subtype classification, this review focuses on how emerging single-cell and spatial multi-omics technologies redefine TAM ontogeny, phenotypic diversity, spatial organization, and therapeutic vulnerabilities. This review summarizes how fate-mapping, single-cell transcriptomics, and spatial multi-omics have contributed to the understanding of the dual origins of TAMs, including embryo-derived tissue-resident macrophages and monocyte-derived macrophages, and how these technologies further delineate transcriptionally and functionally distinct TAM subsets such as SPP1+, TREM2+, C1QC+, and MMP9+ TAMs with context-dependent roles in immune regulation, metastasis, and treatment resistance. We then integrate spatial transcriptomics, multiplex imaging, and radiomics evidence to outline TAM-enriched niches at hypoxic cores, invasive fronts, perivascular regions and tertiary lymphoid structures, emphasizing how these niches coordinate crosstalk among cancer cells, T cells, cancer-associated fibroblasts, endothelial cells and B cells. Emerging TAM-related gene signatures and multi-omics-based scores were further highlighted that predict response or resistance to radiotherapy, chemotherapy, anti-angiogenic therapy, and immune checkpoint blockade. Finally, we provide a forward-looking perspective on strategies to reprogram, deplete, or redirect specific TAM subsets, including CSF1/CSF1R and CCR2/CCL2 blockade, metabolic and epigenetic modulators, agonists of phagocytosis, and CAR-macrophage-based therapies. Overall, we propose that integrating single-cell and spatial omics with AI-assisted digital pathology and longitudinal sampling will enable TAM-informed patient stratification and rational design of combination immunotherapies, thereby accelerating the translation of TAM biology into precision oncology.

doi:10.1038/s41698-026-01643-3.abstract: Clinical translation of T cell bispecific (TCB) therapies in solid tumors is hindered by the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment and intratumoral heterogeneity, features poorly captured by standard preclinical models. We applied an integrated translational framework, combining humanized mouse models, a patient-derived ex vivo organ culture (EVOC) platform, and Phase 1 clinical trial data (ClinTrials.gov identifier NCT03539484), to define the biologic determinants of functional reactivity to a CEACAM5 x CD3 TCB. In humanized mice bearing CEA-positive tumors, the TCB inhibited tumor growth and increased intratumoral T cell infiltration. EVOC, which preserves native 3D tumor architecture and endogenous tumor immune contexture, revealed rapid TCB-induced secretion of IFNγ, IL-2, TNFα, and IL-10 across colorectal, pancreatic, and non-small cell lung cancer patient tumors, with substantial inter-patient heterogeneity. Higher baseline CD3+ T cell infiltration trended with a greater magnitude of cytokine release in patient tumors treated with the TCB ex vivo versus tumors with lower CD3+ T cell infiltration. Baseline tumor CEA expression did not associate with functional response in EVOC. In the Phase 1 trial, on-treatment peripheral cytokine induction was greater in patients with immune-inflamed or -excluded tumors as compared to those with immune-desert tumors. EVOC recapitulated the high inter-patient functional heterogeneity observed clinically, with a coefficient of variation for IFNγ of 135% in EVOC versus 190% in patients, compared with 52% in humanized mice. These findings suggest that early pharmacodynamic responses to CEACAM5 x CD3 TCB associate with a pre-existing tumor immune state rather than target antigen expression alone and support integration of patient-derived ex vivo models for modeling clinically-relevant pharmacodynamics.

doi:10.1038/s41698-026-01674-w.abstract: The tumour microenvironment comprises a variety of cell types that interact with malignant cells, influencing both cancer progression and the patient response to therapy. Given the intricate interactions among these components, assessing how signalling pathways contribute to cancer progression by acting on different components of the TME is particularly complex. Multiplexed imaging allows simultaneous assessment of signalling in multiple of these components. Here, we utilise a highly multiplexed dataset of 61 markers across 746 colorectal tumours to investigate how complex mTOR signalling in different tissue compartments influences patient prognosis. We found that mTOR pathway signalling in immune cells correlates with favourable patient survival. Advanced spatially-aware analysis of signalling activities using graph neural networks revealed that the positive association between immune mTOR signalling and patient survival was more pronounced in tumours with features of a more differentiated morphology. Integrative analysis using TCGA data and spatial transcriptomics confirmed a role for immune mTOR signalling in immune activation, accompanied by reduced TGF-β signalling. Our work highlights the importance of adopting a personalised approach to targeting mTOR in cancer patients and establishes a framework for studying cell type-specific signalling in the TME.

doi:10.1038/s41698-026-01715-4.abstract: Abstract Radiotherapy (RT) transforms tumors into in situ vaccines that trigger antitumor immunity. However, the relevant pathways remain largely unelucidated, limiting clinical translation. Herein, we developed a hybrid dry-lab/wet-lab approach integrating systems-level immune phenotypes following homogenous or spatially fractionated RT (SFRT) with transcriptomic profiling of irradiated tumors. By combining feature extraction with machine-learning, including multilayer perceptron modeling, we ranked predictors of immune infiltration and patient survivability for each RT type. RT induced coordinated upregulation of viral RNA-binding proteins (OASes and RIG I-like receptors) along with endogenous retrovirus (ERV) RNAs predominately 400–800 bp long, which may serve as their ligands. During abscopal responses, OASes and ERV transcripts were co-induced and shared between irradiated and distant tumors. SFRT triggered earlier activation of OAS signaling versus homogenous RT. Our findings highlight ERVs as underappreciated contributors to RT-induced antitumor immunity and their interactions with intratumoral cytosolic sensors as potential novel biomarkers in precision radio-oncology.

doi:10.1038/s41698-026-01730-5.abstract: Abstract Ewing sarcoma (EwS) is an aggressive malignancy of children, adolescents, and young adults driven by the EWS::FLI1 fusion oncoprotein with few effective treatment options in the relapsed or refractory setting. We validate six transmembrane epithelial antigen of the prostate 1 (STEAP1) as a fusion-regulated and clinically actionable surface antigen with broad expression across a series of primary EwS tumors. Analysis of EWS::FLI1 perturbation in EwS models demonstrated regulation of STEAP1 transcript and protein expression by oncogenic EWS::FLI1. Second-generation STEAP1 CAR T cells induced complete tumor regression in orthotopic models and exhibited dose-dependent activity in disseminated disease without evidence of antigen escape. Armoring STEAP1 CAR T cells with IL-18 further potentiated antitumor efficacy, achieving complete responses without overt toxicity in approximately 80% of mice at a five-fold lower cell dose where unarmored STEAP1 CAR T cells were ineffective. Notably, adoptive transfer of autologous STEAP1 CAR T cells is currently being evaluated in a first-in-human phase I/II clinical trial in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (NCT06236139) and the compelling preclinical data presented here support clinical translation to relapsed/refractory EwS.

doi:10.1038/s41698-026-01733-2.abstract: Abstract Patients with multiple myeloma accumulate hundreds of clinical documents over years of sequential therapy, and every treatment decision depends on synthesis across that history. Whether large language model–based systems can match expert agreement on this task, and where they fail, has not been established. On longitudinal records of 811 patients treated over 25 years (44,962 documents and 1,334,677 laboratory values), an agentic reasoning system guided by an indexed clinical skill library was compared against single-pass retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), iterative RAG, iterative RAG augmented with the same skill library, and full-context input on 469 expert-adjudicated patient-question pairs, with an exploratory cross-dataset evaluation on MIMIC-IV. The skill-guided agent exceeded the ceiling at which iterative RAG (75.7%) and full-context input (75.8%) converged, reaching 80.1% concordance, with its advantage widening on the most complex tasks (+11.2 percentage points) and longest records. Providing the same skill library to iterative RAG matched the agent in aggregate (79.0%) and on shorter records, whereas the agent retained a significant advantage on the longest records (+10.3 percentage points in the top decile, p = 0.017) and a numerical, non-significant advantage on the most complex questions (+5.4 percentage points). The aggregate error rate (12.2%) was comparable to expert disagreement (13.6%), but a higher proportion of system errors were clinically significant (57.8 versus 18.8%).

doi:10.1038/s41698-026-01736-z.abstract: Acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) exhibits molecular and metabolic heterogeneity that limits therapeutic efficacy. Although antimetabolites remain central to ALL treatment, determinants of therapeutic sensitivity and resistance remain incompletely understood. Here, we investigated the activity and molecular response landscape of the purine analog triciribine (TCN) across diverse ALL models using integrated phosphoproteomics, thermal proteome profiling, and quantitative proteomics. TCN showed potent cytotoxicity across ALL cell lines and a drug response profile distinct from canonical PI3K-Akt-mTOR inhibitors. Early phosphoproteomics revealed no consistent suppression of Akt pathway signaling, with transient activation of several Akt-associated readouts and inhibition of cyclin-dependent kinase signaling. The monophosphorylated metabolite TCN-P was the predominant intracellular active species, and adenosine kinase (ADK) was required for TCN-P generation and cytotoxicity. Proteome Integral Solubility Alteration profiling identified candidate TCN-P interactions involving nucleotide metabolism, DNA replication, and protein synthesis, associated with impaired purine biosynthesis, DNA damage, translational stress, and cell-cycle perturbation. Across ALL cell lines and primary samples, ADK levels correlated positively with TCN sensitivity, supporting ADK-dependent metabolism as a major determinant of therapeutic response. Together, these findings identify TCN as a metabolically activated antileukemic agent with broad antimetabolite activity and nominate ADK as a potential predictive biomarker for precision therapy in ALL.

doi:10.1038/s41698-026-01756-9.abstract: Missed genetic deletions can prevent cancer patients from receiving effective targeted therapy. Standard pipelines, such as TSO500, use bin count averaging for copy number variation detection but often overlook focal events. To address this, we developed a machine learning (ML) pipeline for deletion detection and zygosity evaluation within the MASTERsg precision oncology program. We focused on the tumor suppressor gene PTEN, whose loss confers sensitivity to mTOR/Akt inhibition. An Extreme Gradient Boosting model trained on PTEN-deleted and wild-type tumor samples identified focal deletions missed by the TSO500 pipeline and CNVkit that were associated with concordant PTEN protein loss by immunohistochemistry. Importantly, the model detected PTEN deletions in 33/204 profiled samples that were classified as PTEN wild-type by TSO500; 75% (15/20) of stainable cases showed absent or reduced PTEN protein expression. These findings demonstrate the potential of ML to enhance panel sequencing, uncovering therapeutically relevant alterations missed by established diagnostic methods.

doi:10.1038/s41698-026-01763-w.abstract: Abstract Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) and BRAF/MEK kinase inhibitors have substantially improved survival in advanced melanoma; however, therapeutic resistance and severe toxicities underscore the ongoing need for alternative strategies. Here, we evaluate the clinical utility of multi-omic profiling, biomarker-stratified recommendations, and survival outcomes within a prospective cohort of 98 patients with advanced cutaneous or uveal melanoma evaluated by the Molecular Tumor Board Freiburg (MTB-FR) between 2021 and 2024. Completed profiling revealed at least one potential actionable target beyond classical BRAF V600 mutations in 83.8% of cases. Alterations in NRAS , atypical BRAF variants, CDK4/6 pathway amplifications, and DNA-damage response (DDR) gene mutations most frequently guided board recommendations. Biomarker-stratified therapies were recommended for 68.4% of patients, and personalized immunotherapy combinations for 72.4%. The treatment implementation rate was 33.8% (n = 27), achieving an overall disease control rate (DCR) of 42.9% and an overall response rate (ORR) of 10.7%. These findings demonstrate that comprehensive molecular profiling in a real-world setting uncovers actionable alterations, providing viable subsequent treatment avenues that may optimize outcomes for heavily pretreated melanoma patients beyond established standards of care. Ultimately, prospective, randomized, biomarker-driven trials remain essential to validate whether these individualized diagnostic strategies translate into a reproducible survival benefit.

doi:10.1038/s43018-021-00292-8.abstract: Abstract Anti-PD-1 treatment has shown unprecedented clinical success in the treatment of non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Here, we performed temporal single-cell RNA and paired T-cell receptor sequencing on 47 tumor biopsies from 36 patients with NSCLC following PD-1-based therapies. We observed increased levels of precursor exhausted T (Texp) cells in responsive tumors after treatment, characterized by low expression of coinhibitory molecules and high expression of GZMK . By contrast, nonresponsive tumors failed to accumulate Texp cells. Our data suggested that Texp cells were unlikely to be derived from the reinvigoration of terminally exhausted cells; instead, they were accumulated by (1) local expansion and (2) replenishment by peripheral T cells with both new and pre-existing clonotypes, a phenomenon we named clonal revival. Our study provides insights into mechanisms underlying PD-1-based therapies, implicating clonal revival and expansion of Texp cells as steps to improve NSCLC treatment.

doi:10.1038/s43018-022-00356-3.abstract: Abstract Inferring single-cell compositions and their contributions to global gene expression changes from bulk RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) datasets is a major challenge in oncology. Here we develop Bayesian cell proportion reconstruction inferred using statistical marginalization (BayesPrism), a Bayesian method to predict cellular composition and gene expression in individual cell types from bulk RNA-seq, using patient-derived, scRNA-seq as prior information. We conduct integrative analyses in primary glioblastoma, head and neck squamous cell carcinoma and skin cutaneous melanoma to correlate cell type composition with clinical outcomes across tumor types, and explore spatial heterogeneity in malignant and nonmalignant cell states. We refine current cancer subtypes using gene expression annotation after exclusion of confounding nonmalignant cells. Finally, we identify genes whose expression in malignant cells correlates with macrophage infiltration, T cells, fibroblasts and endothelial cells across multiple tumor types. Our work introduces a new lens to accurately infer cellular composition and expression in large cohorts of bulk RNA-seq data.

doi:10.1038/s43018-022-00463-1.abstract: Abstract The pancreatic tumor microenvironment drives deregulated nutrient availability. Accordingly, pancreatic cancer cells require metabolic adaptations to survive and proliferate. Pancreatic cancer subtypes have been characterized by transcriptional and functional differences, with subtypes reported to exist within the same tumor. However, it remains unclear if this diversity extends to metabolic programming. Here, using metabolomic profiling and functional interrogation of metabolic dependencies, we identify two distinct metabolic subclasses among neoplastic populations within individual human and mouse tumors. Furthermore, these populations are poised for metabolic cross-talk, and in examining this, we find an unexpected role for asparagine supporting proliferation during limited respiration. Constitutive GCN2 activation permits ATF4 signaling in one subtype, driving excess asparagine production. Asparagine release provides resistance during impaired respiration, enabling symbiosis. Functionally, availability of exogenous asparagine during limited respiration indirectly supports maintenance of aspartate pools, a rate-limiting biosynthetic precursor. Conversely, depletion of extracellular asparagine with PEG–asparaginase sensitizes tumors to mitochondrial targeting with phenformin.

doi:10.1038/s43018-022-00470-2.abstract: Abstract Solid tumors are generally characterized by an acidic tumor microenvironment (TME) that favors cancer progression, therapy resistance and immune evasion. By single-cell RNA-sequencing analysis in individuals with pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), we reveal solute carrier family 4 member 4 (SLC4A4) as the most abundant bicarbonate transporter, predominantly expressed by epithelial ductal cells. Functionally, SLC4A4 inhibition in PDAC cancer cells mitigates the acidosis of the TME due to bicarbonate accumulation in the extracellular space and a decrease in lactate production by cancer cells as the result of reduced glycolysis. In PDAC-bearing mice, genetic or pharmacological SLC4A4 targeting improves T cell-mediated immune response and breaches macrophage-mediated immunosuppression, thus inhibiting tumor growth and metastases. In addition, Slc4a4 targeting in combination with immune checkpoint blockade is able to overcome immunotherapy resistance and prolong survival. Overall, our data propose SLC4A4 as a therapeutic target to unleash an antitumor immune response in PDAC.

doi:10.1038/s43018-022-00475-x.abstract: Abstract Recent longitudinal studies of glioblastoma (GBM) have demonstrated a lack of apparent selection pressure for specific DNA mutations in recurrent disease. Single-cell lineage tracing has shown that GBM cells possess a high degree of plasticity. Together this suggests that phenotype switching, as opposed to genetic evolution, may be the escape mechanism that explains the failure of precision therapies to date. We profiled 86 primary-recurrent patient-matched paired GBM specimens with single-nucleus RNA, single-cell open-chromatin, DNA and spatial transcriptomic/proteomic assays. We found that recurrent GBMs are characterized by a shift to a mesenchymal phenotype. We show that the mesenchymal state is mediated by activator protein 1. Increased T-cell abundance at recurrence was prognostic and correlated with hypermutation status. We identified tumor-supportive networks of paracrine and autocrine signals between GBM cells, nonmalignant neuroglia and immune cells. We present cell-intrinsic and cell-extrinsic targets and a single-cell multiomics atlas of GBM under therapy.

doi:10.1038/s43018-023-00548-5.abstract: Abstract One key barrier to improving efficacy of personalized cancer immunotherapies that are dependent on the tumor antigenic landscape remains patient stratification. Although patients with CD3 + CD8 + T cell-inflamed tumors typically show better response to immune checkpoint inhibitors, it is still unknown whether the immunopeptidome repertoire presented in highly inflamed and noninflamed tumors is substantially different. We surveyed 61 tumor regions and adjacent nonmalignant lung tissues from 8 patients with lung cancer and performed deep antigen discovery combining immunopeptidomics, genomics, bulk and spatial transcriptomics, and explored the heterogeneous expression and presentation of tumor (neo)antigens. In the present study, we associated diverse immune cell populations with the immunopeptidome and found a relatively higher frequency of predicted neoantigens located within HLA-I presentation hotspots in CD3 + CD8 + T cell-excluded tumors. We associated such neoantigens with immune recognition, supporting their involvement in immune editing. This could have implications for the choice of combination therapies tailored to the patient’s mutanome and immune microenvironment.

doi:10.1038/s43018-023-00566-3.abstract: Abstract The immune-specialized environment of the healthy brain is tightly regulated to prevent excessive neuroinflammation. However, after cancer development, a tissue-specific conflict between brain-preserving immune suppression and tumor-directed immune activation may ensue. To interrogate potential roles of T cells in this process, we profiled these cells from individuals with primary or metastatic brain cancers via integrated analyses on the single-cell and bulk population levels. Our analysis revealed similarities and differences in T cell biology between individuals, with the most pronounced differences observed in a subgroup of individuals with brain metastasis, characterized by accumulation of CXCL13 -expressing CD39 + potentially tumor-reactive T (pTRT) cells. In this subgroup, high pTRT cell abundance was comparable to that in primary lung cancer, whereas all other brain tumors had low levels, similar to primary breast cancer. These findings indicate that T cell-mediated tumor reactivity can occur in certain brain metastases and may inform stratification for treatment with immunotherapy.

doi:10.1038/s43018-023-00576-1.abstract: Abstract Precision medicine is critically dependent on better methods for diagnosing and staging disease and predicting drug response. Histopathology using hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained tissue (not genomics) remains the primary diagnostic method in cancer. Recently developed highly multiplexed tissue imaging methods promise to enhance research studies and clinical practice with precise, spatially resolved single-cell data. Here, we describe the ‘Orion’ platform for collecting H&E and high-plex immunofluorescence images from the same cells in a whole-slide format suitable for diagnosis. Using a retrospective cohort of 74 colorectal cancer resections, we show that immunofluorescence and H&E images provide human experts and machine learning algorithms with complementary information that can be used to generate interpretable, multiplexed image-based models predictive of progression-free survival. Combining models of immune infiltration and tumor-intrinsic features achieves a 10- to 20-fold discrimination between rapid and slow (or no) progression, demonstrating the ability of multimodal tissue imaging to generate high-performance biomarkers.

doi:10.1038/s43018-024-00781-6.abstract: Abstract Despite tremendous progress in precision oncology, adaptive resistance mechanisms limit the long-term effectiveness of molecularly targeted agents. Here we evaluated the pharmacological profile of MTX-531 that was computationally designed to selectively target two key resistance drivers, epidermal growth factor receptor and phosphatidylinositol 3-OH kinase (PI3K). MTX-531 exhibits low-nanomolar potency against both targets with a high degree of specificity predicted by cocrystal structural analyses. MTX-531 monotherapy uniformly resulted in tumor regressions of squamous head and neck patient-derived xenograft (PDX) models. The combination of MTX-531 with mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase or KRAS-G12C inhibitors led to durable regressions of BRAF -mutant or KRAS -mutant colorectal cancer PDX models, resulting in striking increases in median survival. MTX-531 is exceptionally well tolerated in mice and uniquely does not lead to the hyperglycemia commonly seen with PI3K inhibitors. Here, we show that MTX-531 acts as a weak agonist of peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor-γ, an attribute that likely mitigates hyperglycemia induced by PI3K inhibition. This unique feature of MTX-531 confers a favorable therapeutic index not typically seen with PI3K inhibitors.

doi:10.1038/s43018-025-00976-5.abstract: Abstract DNA methylation-based classification of (brain) tumors has emerged as a powerful and indispensable diagnostic technique. Initial implementations used methylation microarrays for data generation, while most current classifiers rely on a fixed methylation feature space. This makes them incompatible with other platforms, especially different flavors of DNA sequencing. Here, we describe crossNN, a neural network-based machine learning framework that can accurately classify tumors using sparse methylomes obtained on different platforms and with different epigenome coverage and sequencing depth. It outperforms other deep and conventional machine learning models regarding accuracy and computational requirements while still being explainable. We use crossNN to train a pan-cancer classifier that can discriminate more than 170 tumor types across all organ sites. Validation in more than 5,000 tumors profiled on different platforms, including nanopore and targeted bisulfite sequencing, demonstrates its robustness and scalability with 99.1% and 97.8% precision for the brain tumor and pan-cancer models, respectively.

doi:10.1038/s43018-026-01229-9.abstract: Abstract Recent studies demonstrate that the gut mycobiota plays a key role in several tumors. However, the contribution of commensal fungi to prostate cancer initiation and progression remains understudied. Here we find that Nakaseomyces glabratus is enriched in fecal, blood and tumor samples of patients with castration-resistant prostate cancer, correlating with patients’ poor overall survival. Oral administration of N. glabratus to castrated mice accelerated cancer progression by promoting infiltration and activation of polymorphonuclear myeloid-derived suppressor cells (PMN-MDSCs). Mechanistically, androgen deprivation therapy increases intestinal permeability, resulting in the leakage of N. glabratus from the gut to the tumor site, activating PMN-MDSCs via the Dectin-2 receptor. Treatment of mice with a negatively charged intestinal hydrogel blocks N. glabratus translocation to tumor, reducing PMN-MDSCs’ intratumoral infiltration and activation. Taken together, these findings reveal that the gut-to-tumor translocation of N. glabratus contributes to endocrine resistance in prostate cancer by enhancing the immunosuppressive microenvironment of these tumors.

doi:10.1038/s43018-026-01232-0.abstract: A major barrier to cancer therapy is the emergence of drug-tolerant states that allow tumor cells to bypass the targeted pathway. These refractory states arise through reversible cellular plasticity, a process that also occurs during development and regeneration, giving rise to new lineages or phenotypes and restoring drug sensitivity upon treatment withdrawal. Over time, genetic mutations may accumulate, leading to permanent resistance. This paradigm expands the focus from targeting genetic mechanisms alone to also exploiting nongenetic vulnerabilities, driving clinical strategies that prevent or eliminate plastic and transformed populations. Here, we provide an overview of nongenetic plasticity mechanisms and their emerging clinical applications.

doi:10.1053/j.gastro.2026.08.025.abstract: Primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) is a chronic cholestatic liver disease associated with progressive fibrosis, cirrhosis, liver transplantation, and premature mortality. Despite effective therapies, important challenges remain in the diagnosis and management of PBC, including identification of antimitochondrial antibody-negative disease, assessment of response to ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA), risk stratification, treatment of patients with inadequate response, management of cholestatic pruritus, and prevention of recurrent disease after liver transplantation. The aim of this guideline was to develop evidence-based recommendations addressing these key areas of clinical care. The American Gastroenterological Association (AGA) and the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases (AASLD) convened a multidisciplinary panel to develop clinical practice recommendations for adults with PBC. Systematic reviews were performed for 6 prioritized clinical questions. The Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation framework was used to prioritize clinical outcomes and assess evidence, and its Evidence to Decision Framework was used to develop recommendations. The guideline panel agreed on 6 recommendations. These recommendations address the use of PBC-specific antinuclear antibodies in antimitochondrial antibody-negative suspected PBC, UDCA as first-line therapy, liver stiffness measurement for prognostication, peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor agonists for patients with inadequate response or intolerance to UDCA, linerixibat for moderate to severe pruritus, and UDCA prophylaxis post-transplantation to reduce disease recurrence. The certainty of evidence ranged from moderate to very low. The guideline emphasizes early diagnosis, optimization of first-line therapy, risk-based treatment escalation, symptom management, and prevention of post-transplantation disease recurrence to improve patient outcomes and quality of life.

doi:10.1053/j.gastro.2026.09.025.abstract: Chronic pancreatitis (CP) is a progressive fibroinflammatory disease with rising global incidence and no curative therapy. Gut dysbiosis has been associated with CP, but its causal contribution to disease pathogenesis remains unclear. We intended to identify specific pathogenic microbial species that promote CP and to delineate the underlying pathogenic mechanisms. Multi-omics analyses were used to identify key microbial signatures in CP patients and mice. Novel pathogenic Escherichia coli strains were isolated and bioengineered for functional studies. In vitro and in vivo assays, along with macrophage-specific knockout mice, adenoviral tools, and pharmacological inhibitors, were employed to dissect host-microbe mechanistic pathways. Therapeutic intervention included administering a screened next-generation probiotic. Metagenomic sequencing identified HtpG-high-expressing E. coli (HHEC) enrichment as a dominant microbial signature in CP patients. Prevention of HHEC adherence and colonization alleviated CP, whereas recolonization with a new patient-derived HHEC strain PS718 exacerbated it. Mechanistically, E. coli-derived HtpG upregulated protein arginine methyltransferase 5 (PRMT5) in pancreatic macrophages. Pharmacological inhibition of PRMT5 or macrophage-specific deletion of PRMT5 mitigated pancreatic fibrosis and CP progression. PRMT5 methylated Krüppel-like factor 4 (KLF4) at residues R387/R389, stabilizing it, which promoted M2 polarization and pancreatic fibrosis. Therapeutic intervention with Akkermansia muciniphila, which is reduced in CP, suppressed HHEC colonization and ameliorated CP. These findings provide novel evidence for a pathogenic HHEC-HtpG-macrophage axis in CP, highlighting the potential of microbiota-targeted therapies for the condition.

doi:10.1053/j.gastro.2026.09.026.abstract: Excessive accumulation of extracellular matrix (ECM) derived from human intestinal myofibroblasts (HIMF) drives the significant clinical problem of intestinal fibrosis. Fibrosis is believed to progress even in the absence of intestinal inflammation. ECM-bound transglutaminase 2 (TG2) enzyme may exert direct pro-fibrotic effects. We investigated the role of TG2 in intestinal fibrosis. TG2 expression and activity in human intestinal tissue and HIMF from strictured Crohn's disease (CDs), and controls were measured. ECM accumulation by HIMF in presence or absence of TG2 inhibitors was determined. Putative TG2 signaling pathways discovered in HIMF using bulk RNA sequencing (bulk-RNAseq) and single cell RNA sequencing (scRNAseq) were functionally validated. Role of TG2 in vivo was confirmed using inducible global knockout of TGM2 (encoding TG2) in two experimental fibrosis models. TG activity was increased in CDs compared to controls, with up to 100% activity attributable to TG2. TG activity correlated with the degree of histopathologic tissue fibrosis. HIMF were the major source of TG2, with ≥95% of HIMF TG activity being derived from TG2. Tissue distribution of TG2 in myofibroblasts was confirmed by scRNAseq analysis. Selective inhibition of TG2 activity reduced fibronectin (FN), collagen (COL)I, III and VI accumulation by HIMF. Novel TG2 signaling pathways revealed by bulk-RNAseq, were functionally validated. Inducible TGM2 knockout prevented experimental fibrosis without affecting the degree of intestinal inflammation. TG2 may be involved in inflammation-independent progression of intestinal fibrosis.

doi:10.1053/j.gastro.2026.09.027.abstract: Gemcitabine remains a cornerstone of systemic therapy for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) but acquired resistance limits its efficacy. While both microenvironment-derived metabolites and intrinsic metabolic reprogramming have been implicated in gemcitabine resistance, the relationship between these mechanisms remains poorly understood. We investigated the metabolic adaptations accompanying acquired gemcitabine resistance and identified therapeutically actionable vulnerabilities. Acquired gemcitabine-resistant PDAC models were generated and characterized. The effects of physiological pyrimidines on gemcitabine response were evaluated alongside changes in pyrimidine metabolism. Sensitivity to inhibition of the mevalonate pathway was assessed in vitro and in immunocompetent mouse models. Metabolite rescue experiments were performed to identify critical downstream mediators of statin activity and HMGCR expression was analyzed for its association with clinical response to gemcitabine. PDAC cells with acquired gemcitabine resistance exhibited diminished sensitivity to physiological extracellular pyrimidines due to suppression of the pyrimidine salvage pathway. This metabolic rewiring created a selective dependency on the mevalonate biosynthesis pathway, rendering gemcitabine resistant cells highly sensitive to statins. Statin treatment selectively inhibited the growth of gemcitabine-resistant tumors in mice. Metabolite rescue studies identified geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate depletion, not cholesterol limitation, as a principal mediator of statin sensitivity. HMGCR expression declined progressively during the acquisition of gemcitabine resistance and low HMGCR expression levels predicted poor response to gemcitabine-based therapy in PDAC patients. Acquired gemcitabine resistance drives metabolic reprogramming that suppresses pyrimidine salvage while creating a therapeutically exploitable dependence on the mevalonate pathway. These findings identify pharmacological inhibition of HMGCR as a metabolic vulnerability in gemcitabine resistance and support HMGCR expression as a candidate biomarker for treatment stratification in PDAC patients.

doi:10.1053/j.gastro.2026.09.028.abstract: Dietary fibers modulate host-microbiota interactions. Whether fiber promotes epithelial repair through microbiota-dependent mechanisms remains unclear. We determined how alginate influences colitis recovery and whether the pathway is relevant to ulcerative colitis (UC). We screened fibers in dextran sodium sulfate (DSS)-induced murine colitis and assessed survival, inflammation, barrier function, and epithelial regeneration. Microbiota dependence was evaluated using antibiotics and bacterial supplementation. Metabolites were profiled using capillary electrophoresis-time-of-flight mass spectrometry (CE-TOFMS), and epithelial programs were analyzed using RNA-seq and colonic organoid injury assays. Slc6a6-/- and Cyp2c55-/- mice were used to determine mechanistic requirements. Translational relevance was examined in a randomized, placebo-controlled trial of UC patients receiving antibiotic-primed fecal microbiota transplantation (A-FMT) followed by alginate or placebo. Clinical outcomes, histology, fecal taurine, and colonic CYP2C18 expression were assessed. Alginate improved DSS colitis recovery, reducing inflammation, restoring barrier integrity, and enhancing crypt proliferation. Alginate enriched taurine-releasing bacteria, including Bacteroides acidifaciens and Ligilactobacillus murinus, and increased intestinal taurine; antibiotic disruption abrogated these effects. Taurine was required for benefit, as alginate failed in Slc6a6-/- mice. Alginate and taurine induced epithelial Cyp2c55, and protection was lost in Cyp2c55-/- mice and organoids. In the clinical trial, the primary endpoint was not met. However, alginate supplementation was associated with biological changes, including fecal taurine levels and colonic CYP2C18 expression, consistent with preclinical mechanisms. Alginate engages a fiber-microbiota-taurine-epithelial signaling pathway that promotes recovery in preclinical models. The clinical trial did not meet its primary endpoint; however, the biological changes warrant further investigation of alginate as a microbiota-targeted intervention. jRCTs031200103 (https://jrct.mhlw.go.jp/), registered September 1, 2020: UMIN000041968 (https://www.umin.ac.jp/ctr/index.htm), October 1, 2020.

doi:10.1053/j.jvca.2026.08.146.abstract: Mitral valve repair (MVr) is the ideal treatment strategy for degenerative mitral regurgitation. Mitral valve replacement (MVR) may be required if MVr is unsuccessful during the index surgery. The consequences of MVR following failed MVr during the same surgery are unclear. Retrospective observational study. Single institution, university affiliated. All patients who underwent MVR from 2010 through 2024 were included. Patients with concomitant surgeries were included. Patients were dichotomized into the intended repair (IR) or de novo replacement (DR) groups based on the intended procedure. A total of 1,661 patients (mean age, 64 years; 57% female) underwent MVR. MVr was attempted in 133 patients (8%, IR group), and 1,528 underwent planned MVR (92%, DR group). The mean ejection fraction was 55%. Female sex (58.0% in the DR group v 48.9% in the IR group, p = 0.04), history of infective endocarditis (23.8% v 15.0%, p = 0.02), history of cerebrovascular disease (32.1% v 19.5%, p = 0.03), and prior sternotomy (32.1% v 15.8%, p < 0.001) were more prevalent in the DR group. After propensity score matching, perioperative morbidity and mortality were similar. The median cardiopulmonary bypass time and cross-clamp time were longer in the IR group (207 minutes v 134 minutes in the DR group and 163 minutes v 102 minutes in the DR group, respectively). Kaplan-Meier curve analysis showed similar 5-year survival (p = 0.91). Postoperative outcomes were similar despite longer operative times in the IR group. Failure of initial MVr, leading to MVR, did not translate into adverse early or long-term outcomes. These findings suggest that repair may be more aggressively considered in patients with repairable anatomies.

doi:10.1053/j.jvca.2026.08.167.abstract: To determine whether postoperative mechanical ventilation duration is associated with the risk and timing of visual and auditory hallucinations after adult cardiac surgery. Prospective multicenter cohort study. Ten major cardiac surgery centers in the West Bank, Palestine. A total of 1,332 adults undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting or valve surgery, stratified by postoperative ventilation duration: ≤6 hours or >6 hours. No experimental intervention was performed; patients were grouped by early versus delayed postoperative extubation. Visual and auditory hallucinations were assessed during the first 7 postoperative days using the Questionnaire for Psychotic Experiences. Cox regression and restricted mean survival time analyses evaluated associations between ventilation duration and hallucination outcomes. Delayed extubation (>6 hours) was associated with lower overall adjusted risk of visual hallucinations (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.70; 95% confidence interval, 0.62-0.80; p < .001) and auditory hallucinations (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.49; 95% confidence interval, 0.31-0.77; p = .002). However, time-varying analysis showed increased immediate postoperative hazard in the delayed-extubation group, with risk declining rapidly over time. Restricted mean survival time analysis showed that auditory hallucination-free time was approximately 0.24 days shorter in patients with delayed extubation (p < .001). Preoperative white blood cell count was the most consistent predictor. Delayed postoperative extubation was associated with lower overall 7-day hallucination risk but higher immediate postoperative vulnerability, suggesting that the early postextubation period may represent a critical window for targeted monitoring and preventive neuropsychiatric care after cardiac surgery.

doi:10.1053/j.jvca.2026.08.176.abstract: To compare the prognostic performance of the preoperative C-reactive protein to albumin ratio (CAR), systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), systemic inflammation response index, pan-immune-inflammation value (PIV), and hemoglobin-albumin-lymphocyte-platelet score for predicting mortality after isolated coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) and to determine whether these biomarkers provide incremental prognostic value beyond European System for Cardiac Operative Risk Evaluation (EuroSCORE) II. Retrospective observational cohort study. Single-center tertiary training and research hospital. Six hundred eighteen consecutive adults undergoing isolated CABG between January 1, 2022, and December 1, 2024, with complete 1-year follow-up. None. The primary outcomes were intensive care unit mortality rate (11.8%) and 1-year all-cause mortality rate (16.2%). Among all evaluated biomarkers, CAR demonstrated the strongest prognostic performance for both outcomes and independently predicted in-hospital and 1-year mortality after adjustment for EuroSCORE II and base excess. Incorporating CAR into EuroSCORE II improved discrimination and showed favorable internally validated calibration and decision-curve net benefit within the proposed perioperative management framework, whereas the remaining inflammatory indices provided little or no incremental prognostic information. Cell count-based indices, including SII and PIV, did not demonstrate meaningful prognostic discrimination or independent associations with the evaluated mortality outcomes in the present cohort. The optimal CAR threshold was derived and evaluated within the same cohort and should therefore be considered exploratory pending external validation. Preoperative CAR was independently associated with both in-hospital and 1-year mortality after isolated CABG and provided incremental prognostic information beyond EuroSCORE II in the present cohort. Rather than replacing EuroSCORE II, it provides complementary prognostic information by capturing inflammatory and nutritional dimensions not represented in conventional surgical risk models. External multicenter validation is warranted before routine clinical implementation.

doi:10.1053/j.jvca.2026.09.008.abstract: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people experience significant perioperative health inequity following cardiac surgery. While post-operative outcomes have been summarized in those undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), perioperative cardiac surgical outcomes for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people have not. A literature review was conducted using MEDLINE, Scopus and Embase databases to identify published data comparing post-operative complications in Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander and non-Indigenous Australian adults undergoing cardiac surgery. Selected search terms were used to identify abstracts from eligible studies, which were then screened to identify relevant articles. We identified 15 observational studies examining post-operative complications in Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people undergoing cardiac surgery. Seven focused on isolated CABG, two on isolated valve surgery, and the remainder examined a combination of both. These studies revealed higher post-operative complication rates including myocardial infarction, kidney failure, and long-term mortality among Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people compared to their (frequently >10 year) older non-Indigenous Australian counterparts. Post-CABG, this was largely driven by greater preoperative comorbidity (including higher rates of diabetes mellitus and chronic kidney disease). No studies evaluated pre-operative socioeconomic status, frailty or malnutrition, post-operative self-discharge rates or sepsis, or adjusted analyses of post-operative outcomes following valve surgery. No interventional studies were identified. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people experience greater post-operative morbidity and mortality following cardiac surgery than non-Indigenous Australians. However, further research is warranted to explore several clinically relevant pre-operative variables and post-operative complications, and potential interventions to reduce perioperative inequity in this setting.

doi:10.1053/j.jvca.2026.09.009.abstract: Cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass structurally alters respiratory mechanics and carries a substantial risk of postoperative morbidity. Historically, patients have routinely received conventional oxygen therapy (COT) following extubation. High- flow nasal cannula (HCNC) therapy has emerged as an innovative respiratory support system. By synthesizing all currently available high-quality randomized controlled trials (RCTs), this study aimed to rigorously evaluate the efficacy and safety of HFNC compared to COT, focusing primarily on determining the need for escalation of respiratory support. A thorough electronic search was carried out in the PubMed, Embase, and Scopus databases from their inception to May 2026. Only RCTs were considered for analysis. A random-effects model was applied to compute pooled estimates and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). A total of 11 RCTs, comprising 2473 patients, were included in this systematic review and meta-analysis. HFNC had a statistically significant effect on reducing the requirement for escalation of respiratory support (risk ratio [RR] = 0.71; 95% CI, 0.55-0.93; p = 0.01). HFNC had a statistically significant effect on improving the arterial partial pressure of oxygen, as well as forced expiratory volume in 1 second, while also increasing delirium complications (RR = 3.63; 95% CI, 1.80-7.30; p = 0.0003). There were no statistically significant differences between the 2 approaches in the other secondary clinical and resource utilization outcomes, including intubation, overall mortality, hospital length of stay, intensive care unit length of stay, and postoperative atrial fibrillation. In adult patients recovering from cardiac surgery, HFNC therapy improves oxygenation and significantly curtails the need to escalate respiratory support compared to COT. However, these physiologic and intermediate clinical benefits do not translate into reductions in mortality, reintubation rate, or hospital length of stay and may come at the cost of increased postoperative delirium.

doi:10.1053/j.jvca.2026.09.017.abstract: To evaluate correlations between pressure-based dynamic preload indices and echocardiographic flow velocity variations during coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). Prospective observational pilot study. Single university hospital. Thirty adults undergoing elective CABG. Modified passive leg raising (PLR) at 3 intraoperative time points. Mean arterial pressure increased after PLR at all 3 time points. In pooled analyses, stroke volume variation decreased from 13% ± 4% to 10% ± 4% and pulse pressure variation decreased from 10% ± 2% to 7% ± 3% (both p < 0.05). Respiratory peak velocity variations in the left ventricular outflow tract and descending aorta did not change significantly. Pulse contour-derived cardiac output also did not change (5.1 ± 1.1 L/min v 5.1 ± 1.1 L/min, p = 0.71). Stroke volume variation and pulse pressure variation correlated strongly (r = 0.720), whereas correlations between pressure- and flow-derived indices were weak (r = 0.147-0.351). Pressure-derived indices correlated only weakly with echocardiographic respiratory peak velocity variations in patients undergoing CABG. As forward flow did not measurably increase following modified PLR, the physiological significance of these weak correlations remains uncertain.

doi:10.1053/j.jvca.2026.09.018.abstract: To evaluate the feasibility of continuous bilateral lower-limb near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) monitoring as an adjunct to standard hourly neurovascular assessment (NVA) in patients receiving intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) support, and to characterize the relationship between regional oxygen saturation (rSO₂) and in-hospital mortality. Prospective observational cohort study. Cardiac care unit of a tertiary cardiac center (Tan Tock Seng Hospital, Singapore). Fifty consecutive adult patients receiving IABP support via femoral arterial access. Continuous bilateral lower-limb rSO₂ monitoring using NIRS was performed throughout IABP support, alongside standardized hourly NVA of both limbs (capillary refill time, skin color, temperature, pulse quality, and Doppler signal). Right femoral access was used in 94% of patients (47 of 50). Minimum contralateral (left) rSO₂ was significantly lower in nonsurvivors than survivors (29.3% ± 17.6% v 43.3% ± 14.4%, p = 0.024), with a directionally similar but nonsignificant trend on the ipsilateral (right) side (p = 0.083). Regional oxygen saturation correlated moderately with capillary refill time (Spearman rank correlation [rs] ≈ 0.50) and pulse quality (rs ≈ 0.38) bilaterally but not with temperature change, which deteriorated in >92% of limbs. Low rSO₂ (<40%) in either limb was associated with a nonsignificant 3.16-fold increase in mortality odds (95% confidence interval, 0.55-18.11; p = 0.197). No patient developed acute limb ischemia. Sepsis (odds ratio [OR], 13.0) and renal replacement therapy (OR, 7.1) were the only statistically significant predictors of mortality. Continuous bilateral lower-limb rSO₂ monitoring is feasible throughout IABP support and produces a physiologically coherent signal that correlates moderately with objective NVA parameters and is lower in patients who do not survive to discharge. No limb ischemic events occurred; these findings are best regarded as feasibility and physiology data rather than evidence that continuous monitoring improves limb outcomes, and they warrant confirmation in a larger, multicenter study.

doi:10.1053/j.jvca.2026.09.027.abstract: To compare high-frequency low-tidal volume (HFLTV) ventilation with standard ventilation (SV) regarding procedural efficiency, airway mechanics, and clinical outcomes in atrial fibrillation (AF) catheter ablation. Retrospective, observational, nonrandomized cohort study. Electrophysiology laboratory of a single tertiary-care university hospital. There were 160 consecutive eligible adults undergoing first-time AF radiofrequency ablation under general anesthesia between June 2023 and May 2024. Patients received HFLTV (n = 80; respiratory rate 25-30 breaths/min, tidal volume 3-4 mL/kg, ETCO₂ maintained <50 mmHg) or SV (n = 80; tidal volume 6-8 mL/kg, respiratory rate 10-12 breaths/min) per attending anesthesiologist practice. All received propofol-remifentanil total intravenous anesthesia. Primary outcomes were total procedure time and radiofrequency ablation time; secondary outcomes were airway pressures, oxygenation, AF recurrence at 1 and 6 months, AF-related hospitalization, and complications. HFLTV was associated with lower median procedure time (110 v 128 minutes; p < .001) and ablation time (23 v 28 minutes; p < .001). Peak (14 v 18 cmH₂O) and minimum (13 v 15 cmH₂O) airway pressures were lower with HFLTV (both p < .001), whereas ETCO₂ and SpO₂ nadir were comparable. Multivariable regression identified HFLTV as an independent predictor of shorter ablation time (nonstandardized β=-5.48 minutes; 95% CI -7.05 to -3.91; p < .001). In exploratory analyses, recurrence at 1 month (7.5% v 15.0%; p = .211) and 6 months (13.8% v 18.8%; p = .520) and 6-month AF-related hospitalization (12.5% v 18.8%; p = .384) were numerically lower with HFLTV but confidence intervals were wide and included no difference. In a consecutive cohort including paroxysmal and persistent AF, HFLTV was associated with shorter procedure and ablation times and lower measured airway pressures without compromising gas exchange. Clinical outcome analyses were exploratory and hypothesis-generating, warranting prospective randomized evaluation.

doi:10.1053/j.jvca.2026.09.032.abstract: To evaluate the reliability and readability of responses generated by two artificial intelligence (AI) platforms-ChatGPT and MediSearch-to common patient-focused questions about cardiac surgery and its anesthetic implications. Prospective, comparative, cross-sectional evaluation. Single-institution academic study; no direct patient involvement. Questions were sourced from publicly available online data (Google "People Also Ask" feature). One hundred unique patient-focused questions about cardiac surgery and anesthesia, categorized using the Rothwell classification system (80 fact, 14 policy, 6 value). Each question was submitted individually to the free versions of ChatGPT (version 4.0) and MediSearch. Responses were evaluated using three validated metrics: reliability, assessed using the modified DISCERN tool; readability, assessed using the Flesch-Kincaid grade level (FK) and Coleman-Liau index (CL); and clinical accuracy, assessed by a board-certified cardiothoracic anesthesiologist and a board-certified cardiothoracic surgeon using a 3-point Likert scale. MediSearch demonstrated significantly higher reliability (mean DISCERN score, 4.64 v 2.47; p < 0.001). ChatGPT generated significantly more readable responses (mean FK score, 10.33 v 11.34 [p < 0.01]; mean CL score, 15.72 v 17.30 [p < 0.001]) and significantly higher clinical accuracy (mean, 0.82 v 0.71; p < 0.01). Subgroup analysis by Rothwell category confirmed MediSearch's reliability advantage across all question types, while ChatGPT's readability advantage was most pronounced for fact-based questions. This study reveals a critical trade-off between evidence-based reliability and linguistic accessibility in AI-generated cardiac surgery patient education content. MediSearch offers superior reliability, while ChatGPT provides more readable and accurate responses. Neither platform achieves the sixth-grade readability level recommended for broad public accessibility. These findings underscore the need for AI platforms to balance clinical accuracy with health literacy standards before being endorsed as patient education tools in high-stakes settings.

doi:10.1053/j.jvca.2026.09.035.abstract: Postoperative pain after open cardiac surgery arises from both sternotomy and chest drains and is often inadequately controlled by anatomically limited techniques. This study compared the serratus posterior superior intercostal plane block (SPSIPB, C3-T10 spread) with superficial parasternal intercostal plane block (PSIPB) plus chest drain-site infiltration. Prospective, randomized, controlled trial with blinded outcome assessment. Single-center tertiary referral cardiac surgery center. Adults undergoing elective open cardiac surgery via median sternotomy; 80 assessed for eligibility, 76 randomized. Bilateral SPSIPB (n = 35) or bilateral PSIPB plus local anesthetic infiltration at mediastinal and pleural chest drain sites (n = 41), performed preoperatively under ultrasound guidance. The primary outcome was cumulative 24-hour opioid consumption (morphine milligram equivalents, MME); the registered secondary outcomes were Numerical Rating Scale (NRS) pain scores at rest and on coughing and the Quality of Recovery-15 (QoR-15) at 24 hours. All other comparisons were exploratory. Twelve patients were excluded after randomization (2 SPSIPB, 10 control), leaving 33 and 31 for analysis. Opioid consumption was significantly lower in the SPSIPB group (36.6 ± 17.5 v 56.7 ± 16.1 mg of MME; mean difference 20.1 mg of MME; 95% CI, 11.7-28.5; p < 0.001). NRS scores were comparable during the first postoperative hour but lower in the SPSIPB group from 2 hours onward during coughing and at 4, 8, and 24 hours at rest (all p ≤ 0.019). QoR-15 scores were higher in the SPSIPB group (119 [112-126] v 108 [105-111.5]; median difference 10 points; 95% CI, 6-15; p < 0.001), exceeding the minimal clinically important difference of 6 points. Adverse events, including postoperative nausea and vomiting, did not differ between the groups. Compared with PSIPB plus drain-site infiltration-an active comparator targeting both the sternal and drain regions-SPSIPB reduced opioid consumption and improved quality of recovery and may be a valuable component of multimodal analgesia within Enhanced Recovery After Cardiac Surgery (ERACS) protocols.

doi:10.1053/j.jvca.2026.09.042.abstract: Stenting of the patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) offers a minimally invasive alternative to the modified Blalock-Thomas-Taussig shunt in infants with ductal-dependent pulmonary blood flow. This study reviews the periprocedural management of infants undergoing ductal stenting in the cardiac catheterization laboratory. A retrospective single-center review. Quaternary children's hospital. Infants receiving PDA stents in the cardiac catheterization laboratory from 2018 to 2021 were included. None. Sixty-eight patients were included; median age was 5 days [1-62]; 95.6% (65/68) were neonates and 23.5% (16/68) premature. Pulmonary atresia with intact ventricular septum was the most common cardiac diagnosis (n = 23, 33.8%); 22.1% (15/68) presented with a syndrome and 35.3% (24/68) with noncardiac comorbidities. In total, 39.7% (27/68) developed intraoperative events. Median time to extubation was 19.4 hours [3.2-372.5]. Infants with ductal-dependent pulmonary blood flow undergoing ductal stenting may present with a wide range of challenges in the perioperative period. Meticulous care and interdisciplinary coordination are required to optimize the outcomes for this particularly vulnerable patient group.

doi:10.1053/j.jvca.2026.09.043.abstract: To identify if the delivery of oxygen over consumption of oxygen (DO2/VO2) ratio is significantly associated with clinical outcomes such as mortality, need for heart transplantation, or need for a mechanical circulatory support device. Retrospective cohort study. Medical and surgical cardiac intensive care units of the Mayo Clinic. Adult patients (≥18 years old) admitted to the cardiothoracic surgical or cardiac intensive care units between January 2012 and December 2025 were included if they underwent invasive hemodynamic assessment with simultaneous arterial blood gas, mixed venous blood gas, hemoglobin, and mean arterial pressure. Patients were excluded if they had their venous oxygen saturations drawn from a central line or a peripherally inserted central catheter, as well as those admitted for sepsis/septic shock. No interventions were performed on patients. DO2/VO2 demonstrated a nonlinear association with mortality. Using the median value of 4.73 as a reference point, patients with a DO2/VO2 value of ∼2 had the highest likelihood of mortality. Kaplan-Meier analysis using a prespecified cut-point of 5 did not demonstrate any significant relationship with mortality, likely because of the underlying nonlinear relationship. There was no significant association between DO2/VO2 ratio and the need for mechanical circulatory support or heart transplantation. DO₂/VO₂ is a marker of systemic oxygen balance that complements conventional hemodynamic indices. A categorical threshold of 5 did not show an association with clinical outcomes, but continuous analyses did suggest that a low DO₂/VO₂ may identify a high-risk phenotype.

doi:10.1053/j.jvca.2026.09.044.abstract: To synthesize available evidence on perioperative management and clinical outcomes of hepatectomy in patients with Fontan circulation, focusing on hemodynamic strategies and surgical safety. A systematic review of case reports and case series. Published studies were identified through databases (PubMed, Scopus, Cochrane Library, Google Scholar, ICHUSHI, and CiNii Research). Thirty-one patients from 28 studies underwent hepatectomy after the Fontan procedure. Open or laparoscopic hepatectomy, primarily for hepatocellular carcinoma in the setting of Fontan-associated liver disease. All patients had stable Fontan physiology, and no perioperative mortality was reported. Preoperative baseline central venous pressure (CVP) ranged from 10 to 15 mmHg. Intraoperative management consistently favored a baseline-CVP strategy over conventional low-CVP targets. Laparoscopic approaches uniformly used low-pressure pneumoperitoneum below baseline-CVP levels. The Pringle maneuver was well tolerated; however, inferior vena cava clamping was associated with significant hypotension. The median blood loss was 1,106 mL (range 10-4,130 mL). Congestion-related complications, including ascites, pleural effusion, heart failure, and unspecified fluid retention, were most commonly reported postoperatively. Hepatectomy appears feasible in carefully selected patients with stable Fontan circulation. Practical perioperative considerations summarized from reported patterns include maintaining CVP near baseline, minimizing increases in pulmonary vascular resistance, and keeping pneumoperitoneum pressure below baseline CVP during laparoscopic surgery. However, hepatectomy-specific risk stratification has yet to be established, and optimal perioperative management of patients with impaired Fontan physiology remains uncertain. A critical knowledge gap remains regarding hemostatic approaches that optimize bleeding control while preserving the Fontan circulation.

doi:10.1053/j.jvca.2026.09.049.abstract: To identify preoperative predictors of postoperative renal replacement therapy (RRT) in patients undergoing left ventricular assist device (LVAD) implantation to help guide interventions that could decrease the incidence of new dialysis-dependent acute kidney injury (AKI). Retrospective cohort study. A single-center, university hospital. There were 159 adult patients undergoing LVAD implantation between July 2012 to July 2024 INTERVENTIONS: Retrospective analysis of preoperative variables, including hemoglobin, creatinine, MELD score, and intraoperative RBC transfusion volume and their effect on the primary outcome of new dialysis-dependent AKI. New dialysis-dependent AKI occurred in 17% of patients. Preoperative hemoglobin was inversely associated with RRT risk; every 1-g/dL increase was associated with a 21% reduction in odds ratio (OR 0.79; CI 0.65-0.97, p = .023). Intraoperative red blood cell transfusion volume was a major predictor, with patients receiving 0 to 5 units having significantly lower OR than those receiving ≥11 units (OR 0.01; 95% CI 0.001-0.11; p < .001). MELD scores between 10 and 20 also increased the OR (OR 3.10; 95% CI 1.07-9.00; p = .038). Additionally, needing new dialysis was strongly associated with prolonged mechanical ventilation (OR 8.76; 95% CI 2.52-30.5; p = .001) and postoperative gastrointestinal bleeding (OR 3.73; 95% CI 1.48-9.40; p = .005). Preoperative hemoglobin and perioperative red blood cell transfusion volume are significant and potentially actionable, modifiable risk factors for postoperative RRT in LVAD recipients. Optimizing preoperative hemoglobin may offer a targeted strategy to reduce RRT rates in this high-risk population.

doi:10.1053/j.jvca.2026.09.050.abstract: Sotatercept is a groundbreaking new treatment for pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). The disease-modifying drug is a recombinant fusion protein that consists of the extracellular domain of the activin receptor 2A linked to the Fc fragment of human immunoglobulin G1. Sotatercept potently traps activins and growth differentiation factors to inhibit transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-β) signaling through its activin receptor 2A/2B pathway, thereby restoring the neutral balance between pro-proliferative and antiproliferative signaling in PAH and causing a striking reversal of the disease's pathologic consequences. This article had the following objectives: (1) describe the parallel TGF-β signaling pathways and their opposing effects on pulmonary artery endothelial and smooth muscle cell quiescence and proliferation; (2) discuss the mechanisms by which sotatercept differentially affects TGF-β signaling to inhibit and reverse aberrant vascular proliferation and facilitate cellular quiescence; (3) review the preclinical evidence indicating that sotatercept has favorable actions in experimental models of PAH; (4) examine the findings of major clinical trials and their substudies demonstrating that sotatercept exerts temporally durable benefits on pulmonary and right ventricular hemodynamics, clinical symptoms, exercise tolerance, quality of life, and mortality in patients with long-standing, high-risk, and newly identified PAH; (5) assess recent findings indicating that sotatercept produces salutary actions in patients with precapillary and postcapillary pulmonary hypertension resulting from heart failure with preserved ejection fraction; and lastly, (6) comment on the adverse effects of sotatercept and its potential anesthetic implications.
