doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1957407.abstract: To evaluate 5.0-T ultra-high-field multi-parametric diffusion MRI (mp-dMRI) combined with histogram analysis for assessing the pathological grade, stage, and adverse pathological factors in prostate cancer (PCa). This retrospective study included 138 patients with histopathologically confirmed PCa. All patients underwent preoperative 5.0-T MRI, including diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI), diffusion kurtosis imaging (DKI), and intravoxel incoherent motion (IVIM) sequences. Histogram parameters were extracted from parametric maps of the apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC), mean diffusivity (MD), mean kurtosis (MK), true diffusion coefficient (D), perfusion fraction (f), etc. using 3D Slicer software. Between-group comparisons were performed using the Mann-Whitney U test or the independent-samples t-test, as appropriate. Spearman's rank correlation analysis was used to evaluate the relationships between histogram parameters and both the ISUP grade group (ISUP GG) and pathological T stage (pT). Logistic regression was used for variable selection and model construction. Diagnostic performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. Among the 138 patients, most histogram parameters of ADC, MD, MK, D, and f differed significantly between clinically significant PCa (csPCa) and clinically insignificant PCa (ciPCa). For distinguishing csPCa from ciPCa, D_90th percentile achieved the highest AUC among single parameters (0.756). Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses identified ADC_mean, MD_Minimum, D_90th percentile, and f_Maximum as independent predictors across the DWI, DKI, and IVIM sequences. The combined model comprising these four parameters achieved an AUC of 0.809. After internal validation using bootstrap resampling (1,000 repetitions), the resulting AUC was 0.808, indicating good model robustness. Further correlation analysis showed that multiple histogram parameters of ADC, MD, MK, D, and f also demonstrated mild to moderate correlations with ISUP GG and pT stage. D_RMS and MD_skewness exhibited the strongest correlations with ISUP GG and pT stage, respectively (r = -0.458 and r = 0.443, both P < 0.001). Finally, among the 60 surgical patients, multiple histogram features of ADC, MD, MK, D, and f differed significantly between patients with and without EPE, SVI, PSM, and PNI. Quantitative histogram parameters derived from 5.0-T ultra-high-field mp-dMRI show promise for the non-invasive assessment of tumor aggressiveness and adverse prognostic factors in PCa.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1957469.abstract: Programmable messenger RNA (mRNA) platforms can encode tumor antigens or immunomodulators, enabling coordinated antigen delivery and immune modulation. Yet the literature spans cancer vaccination, delivery engineering, immune biology, and adjacent infectious-disease research, making its structure and evidentiary boundaries difficult to discern. We mapped this cross-domain corpus to clarify its development, organization, and relevance to cancer-associated immune escape. We searched the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC) and Scopus on July 29, 2026, for English-language Articles and Reviews published since 2006. The strategy combined programmable or therapeutic mRNA, cancer, and immune-escape-related concepts. R-based analyses summarized the number of publications (NP), total citations (TC), and collaboration patterns; BERTopic modeled titles and abstracts after entity-aware preprocessing. Independent two-author review supported the five topic labels and characterized the outliers, and robustness was assessed across alternative clustering configurations. The dataset comprised 756 publications (NP = 756). Annual output increased more than fourfold in 2021 and reached NP = 182 in 2025. China (NP = 291; 38.49%) and the United States (NP = 146; 19.31%) accounted for nearly 58% of corresponding-author publications. Sichuan University and Frontiers in Immunology ranked first in institutional and journal output, respectively. Nature had the highest retained source-record citation total (TC = 2,326). BERTopic assigned 745 publications to five topics, while 11 of 756 records remained outliers (1.46%). The topics represented mRNA delivery and immunomodulatory cancer-vaccine research (52.1%), SARS-CoV-2 vaccination in oncology and immunotherapy settings (23.6%), therapeutic mRNA cancer-vaccine platforms (13.3%), tumor-antigen discovery and immune-subtype stratification (8.6%), and mRNA-vaccine immunogenicity during autoimmune immunosuppression (2.4%). Publication activity in the retrieved cross-domain corpus expanded rapidly after 2020. The corpus included both direct cancer-mRNA research and adjacent platform or immune-response literature. By distinguishing these components and identifying thematic connections among delivery, antigen selection, immune context, and collaboration, the analysis provides an evidence-navigation framework for prioritizing systematic reviews, mechanistic studies, and clinical evaluation. The map does not itself establish therapeutic efficacy.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1957728.abstract: Background KRAS-mutated ultra-low rectal cancer is associated with poor response to conventional neoadjuvant therapy, making sphincter preservation particularly challenging. In addition, effective rehabilitation strategies for severe low anterior resection syndrome (LARS) remain limited. Case presentation A 55-year-old woman with KRAS-mutated ultra-low rectal adenocarcinoma experienced insufficient tumor regression after multiple lines of chemotherapy, chemoradiotherapy, and immunotherapy, complicated by oxaliplatin allergy. After referral to our center, she received bevacizumab plus XELIRI combined with traditional Chinese medicine therapies. Following five treatment cycles, the patient underwent laparoscopic radical rectal resection with transanal specimen extraction and Bacon-type pull-through reconstruction. Pathological examination demonstrated negative proximal, distal, and circumferential margins, no metastatic involvement among 12 examined lymph nodes, and a final pathological stage of ypT2N0. The patient subsequently developed major LARS and underwent a four-week rehabilitation program centered on electroacupuncture at the Baliao acupoints. Assessment was conducted using the LARS score, Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center Bowel Function Instrument (MSKCC-BFI), and EORTC QLQ-C30 scales. The patient’s bowel movement frequency decreased from over 30 times per day to approximately 10 times, and remained stable at 7–10 times during the 6-month follow-up. Conclusion In this patient, an individualized conversion strategy was followed by R0 sphincter-preserving resection, and postoperative bowel function improved temporally during and after multimodal rehabilitation that included electroacupuncture. This observation provide preliminary evidence in support of this treatment approach. However, high-quality studies are still required to comprehensively evaluate the efficacy of this treatment regimen.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1959029.abstract: Pancreatic hamartoma (PH) is an exceedingly rare benign non-neoplastic lesion of the pancreas. Owing to its nonspecific clinical and radiological features, it is prone to misdiagnosis. Among its various subtypes, functionally active pancreatic hamartomas with distinct endocrine activity have only been sporadically reported in the literature as individual cases. We report the case of a 58-year-old female patient whose initial presentation was characterized by paroxysmal behavioral abnormalities during nocturnal sleep, manifesting as sudden agitation, arm-flinging, and purposeless stereotyped movements after sleep onset. During these episodes, the patient exhibited a confusional state with subsequent complete amnesia for the events, a clinical phenotype highly suggestive of REM sleep behavior disorder (RBD) or frontal lobe epilepsy. In-hospital monitoring revealed refractory nocturnal hypoglycemia. Imaging studies identified a mass in the pancreatic tail, and the patient underwent laparoscopic distal pancreatectomy. Postoperative histopathological and immunohistochemical examination confirmed the diagnosis of pancreatic hamartoma, composed predominantly of islet cells (approximately 90%) with associated islet cell tumor-like hyperplasia. Following surgery, the patient's nocturnal hypoglycemia and sleep-related behavioral abnormalities resolved completely.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1959240.abstract: The process of chronic gastritis transforming into gastric cancer (GC) follows the classic Correa cascade, with persistent inflammation driving the stepwise transition from normal gastric mucosa through superficial gastritis, atrophic gastritis, intestinal metaplasia, dysplasia, and ultimately carcinoma. Among these stages, intestinal metaplasia and dysplasia occurring on an atrophic mucosal background are widely regarded as the most common gastric precancerous lesions (GPL) because of their pronounced carcinogenic risk. Chronic inflammation can induce epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), thereby accelerating gastric malignant progression. In the GPL stage, the inflammatory gastric microenvironment commonly induces partial EMT (pEMT); importantly, this state is partly reversible and may be amenable to intervention to slow disease progression. As lesions advance, epithelial cells more fully undergo EMT, acquiring greater motility, invasiveness, and metastatic capability, which increases susceptibility to malignant conversion. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are key molecular regulators in the transition from chronic gastritis to GC through EMT modulation. This review comprehensively discusses inflammation-driven EMT activation and functionally classifies pro-EMT oncomiRNAs (e.g., miR-21, miR-155) and anti-EMT tumor-suppressive miRNAs (e.g., miR-200 family, let-7 family, miR-34a), delineating a complex crosstalk network among inflammation, miRNA, and EMT. We further evaluate miRNAs as non-invasive biomarkers for early detection and prognosis of GPL and discuss emerging therapeutic strategies targeting the miRNA-EMT axis, including nanoparticle- or exosome-based delivery systems, miRNA antagonists, and miRNA sponges. Nevertheless, clinical application of circulating miRNAs remains limited by insufficient assay standardization and validation, incomplete target specificity, off-target effects, suboptimal delivery efficiency, and a lack of large-scale clinical evidence. By integrating molecular mechanisms and transformation status of miRNA-EMT axis in GPL, this review provides new insights for precision prevention and targeted intervention in gastric carcinogenesis.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1959542.abstract: Paraptosis is a form of non-apoptotic cell death characterized by cytoplasmic vacuolization and swelling of the mitochondria and endoplasmic reticulum (ER). Recent studies have demonstrated that inducing paraptosis in cancer cells can circumvent apoptosis resistance and synergize with other forms of cell death and tumor immunity, providing a novel strategy for anti-tumor therapy. The underlying mechanism of paraptosis involves ER stress triggered by inducers, leading to the swelling of the ER and mitochondria. This subsequently alters the cytoskeleton and disrupts molecular processes, such as calcium (Ca2+) homeostasis, ultimately causing cytoplasmic vacuolization and cell death. Unlike other forms of programmed cell death, paraptosis is caspase-independent and is marked by mitochondrial and ER swelling, along with extensive cytoplasmic vacuolization, without nuclear pyknosis or cell membrane rupture. Various natural compounds, chemical agents, and nanomedicines have been shown to induce paraptosis, which also holds potential in immunotherapy by promoting immunogenic cell death (ICD) and systemic anti-tumor responses. Thus, in cases where cancer cells evade and develop resistance to conventional pro-apoptotic therapies, paraptosis induction offers an alternative therapeutic approach. A comprehensive understanding of the molecular mechanisms underlying paraptosis and its targeted induction may facilitate the development of novel cancer treatments. This paper explores the impact of paraptosis on cancer cells, the mechanisms by which different drugs induce paraptosis, and the potential applications of paraptosis in cancer therapy.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1959731.abstract: We describe a case of a patient with multiple sclerosis (MS) stable on natalizumab who developed widespread gadolinium-enhancing lesions and clinical relapse seven and eight months after gamma knife radiosurgery (GKRS) for left cerebellar convexity meningioma. We explore how increased blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability post-GKRS could potentially interfere with the lymphocyte anti-trafficking effect of natalizumab and result in new central nervous system (CNS) inflammation distant from the radiation site. Comprehensive analysis of the patient's chart, brain and spine imaging, serum and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) profiles was conducted. We compiled a graphical representation of treatment changes, radiologic findings, and GKRS initiation within one timeframe. We conducted a structured literature review to support the discussion of this case and hypothesize possible pathophysiological mechanisms contributing to clinical and radiological findings. Seven months after GKRS, follow-up brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) demonstrated multiple gadolinium-enhancing lesions in both cerebral hemispheres, and repeat imaging one month later revealed new gadolinium-enhancing lesions, correlating with the patient's clinical relapse. Alternative causes of disease progression, including radiation-induced demyelination, radionecrosis, opportunistic infections, progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML), and development of anti-natalizumab antibodies, were explored and considered less likely. The patient was switched to ofatumumab with subsequent clinical and radiological stability. Given extensive new inflammatory lesions far from the GKRS site, it seems unlikely that the sole mechanism was radiation-induced neurotoxicity. We hypothesize that late delayed radiation side effects caused by GKRS may have enabled peripheral lymphocytes to enter the CNS, counteracting the effects of natalizumab on blocking lymphocyte trafficking through the BBB and possibly contributing to MS relapse.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1959750.abstract: Background Nigeria bears one of the world’s largest burdens of HIV, with ongoing expansion of antiretroviral therapy (ART) significantly improving the survival of people living with HIV (PLHIV). This epidemiologic shift has changed the pattern of morbidity and mortality toward chronic conditions, especially HIV-associated malignancies (HIVAMs), including both AIDS-defining malignancies (ADMs) and non-AIDS-defining malignancies (NADMs). Despite their increasing significance, the national burden, patterns, and systemic challenges related to HIVAMs in Nigeria remain poorly understood and characterized. Methods We conducted a narrative review of peer-reviewed literature, cancer registry reports, and grey literature published between January 2000 and December 2024. Searches were carried out in PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, African Journals Online, and Google Scholar, complemented by national reports from the National Agency for the Control of AIDS, the Federal Ministry of Health, and the National System of Cancer Registries. Eligible sources reported cancer occurrence among PLHIV or HIV prevalence among cancer patients in Nigeria. Findings were synthesized narratively due to significant heterogeneity across study designs and outcomes. Results Seventy-three sources met the inclusion criteria, and these were primarily hospital-based and retrospective studies. ADMs remain the most common cancers among PLHIV, notably invasive cervical cancer, Kaposi sarcoma, and non-Hodgkin lymphoma, with notable regional differences. Expansion of ART has been linked to a decline in Kaposi sarcoma incidence, while the burden of cervical cancer remains high, driven by persistent oncogenic HPV infection and limited screening coverage among women living with HIV (WLWH). Emerging NADMs, such as hepatocellular carcinoma, Hodgkin lymphoma, breast cancer, and ocular surface squamous neoplasia, reflect improved survival, aging, chronic immune dysregulation, and co-infections like Hepatitis B and C. Across these cancers, late-stage presentation and poor outcomes are common, largely due to fragmented HIV–cancer surveillance, inadequate pathology and radiotherapy capacity, limited molecular diagnostics, high out-of-pocket treatment costs, and weak integration of HIV and oncology services. Conclusion HIV-associated cancers pose a major yet often overlooked public health issue in Nigeria. Enhancing integrated HIV–cancer surveillance, increasing prevention and early detection efforts through ART programs, upgrading diagnostic and treatment facilities, and utilizing digital and molecular innovations are essential for decreasing preventable cancer-related morbidity and mortality among PLHIV in Nigeria.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1960445.abstract: Despite the expansion of hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) services, contemporary Total Body Irradiation (TBI) practices remain insufficiently characterized in many healthcare settings. This study aimed to establish a national baseline for TBI practice to support benchmarking, standardization, and quality improvement. A cross-sectional online survey was distributed between May and June 2026 to seven Saudi centers that provided TBI services. The questionnaire collected data on service capacity, patient populations, dose fractionation, treatment techniques and delivery, planning methods, and quality assurance. A census sampling approach was used, inviting Radiation Oncologists, Medical Physicists, and Therapists. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics in Python (v3.11). All seven centers responded. One center (C) submitted two responses covering conventional extended source-to-surface distance (SSD) and volumetric-modulated arc therapy (VMAT) practices. Commissioned between 1980 and 2020, the TBI programs manage an estimated 386 annual cases (range: 12-120). Fractionated TBI (10-12 Gy, six twice-daily fractions) predominated. The extended SSD opposed-beam technique remained in use at six centers, with the umbilicus as the most common prescription point. At two centers, extended-SSD TBI was used alongside Intensity-modulated radiation therapy (IMRT)-TBI (VMAT and Tomotherapy. IMRT-TBI-based centers reported volumetric target-coverage objectives of 90% and explicit organ-at-risk (OAR) dose planning constraints, particularly for the lungs and kidneys. Treatment planning for IMRT-TBI involved treatment planning systems (TPS), whereas extended-SSD techniques used varied planning approaches, including in-house spreadsheets, pre-calculated templates, and, in some cases, TPS-assisted planning. In vivo dosimetry was performed at all centers. The absorbed dose-rate at the prescription point ranged from <10 to 30 cGy/min for conventional techniques. Three centers planned their initial implementation of IMRT-TBI within three years. The ability to control OARs was the main driver, while linear accelerator availability and staff training were key barriers. Although conventional extended SSD TBI remains the most widely used technique, TBI practice is transitioning toward IMRT-based delivery. National practice guidelines based on existing international recommendations may help standardize care, address implementation barriers, and support the delivery of high-quality TBI services across treatment centers.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1960540.abstract: The aims of this study were to explore the longitudinal trajectories of core symptoms in survivors with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) after transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) and to analyze their associations with health-related quality of life (HRQoL) and unmet supportive care needs. This longitudinal study enrolled 271 HCC survivors undergoing TACE in China. Patient-reported outcomes were assessed at three time points-24 h (T1), 7 days (T2), and 1 month (T3) post-TACE-using four validated instruments: the MD Anderson Symptom Inventory-Chinese Version (MDASI-C), the Tumor Symptom Measure for Primary Liver Cancer (TSM-PLC), the Quality of Life Instrument for Liver Cancer (QOL-LC V2.0), and the Short Form of Survivors' Unmet Needs Scale (SF-SUNS). Exploratory factor analysis was conducted to extract discrete symptom clusters, and network analysis was used to calculate strength centrality (rs)-an index quantifying the sum of absolute edge weights connecting each symptom to all others-to identify core symptoms. Five symptom clusters were identified at T1: Fatigue-Cognitive, Post-embolization, Somatic, Emotional, and Hepatobiliary-Specific. The Post-embolization cluster was present only at T1, whereas the remaining four clusters persisted at T2 and T3. However, the core symptom shifted over time: nausea at T1 (rs = 1.154), lack of appetite at T2 (rs = 1.229), and sadness at T3 (rs = 1.107). HRQoL was lowest at T1, improved at T2, and declined at T3, with all pairwise comparisons significant (all p < 0.001). Unmet needs were highest at T3, with all time-point differences significant (all p < 0.001). The largest gaps were observed in information provision, care continuity, and emotional support. Greater symptom severity was significantly associated with poorer HRQoL at all time points (all p < 0.01). During the first month post-TACE, the sequence of core symptoms transitioned from nausea to lack of appetite and then to sadness, suggesting time-specific supportive care strategies-including antiemetic prophylaxis, nutritional support, and psychosocial care. Routine assessment of unmet needs may help reduce symptom burden and optimize long-term HRQoL for these survivors.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1960553.abstract: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) are abundant and functionally diverse components of the lung tumor microenvironment (TME) and are associated with therapeutic response and resistance in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Durable responses to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) and targeted therapies remain limited, with TAM-associated immune evasion and therapy-refractory microenvironments representing potentially relevant components of this resistance landscape. This narrative review prioritizes evidence from human NSCLC specimens and clinically annotated cohorts, especially from single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and spatial transcriptomics, while integrating relevant mechanistic evidence from NSCLC experimental systems, animal models, and related cancer contexts. Moving beyond the M1/M2 paradigm, we synthesize convergent findings to describe recurring, niche-resolved TAM programs. Across NSCLC, we highlight recurrent SPP1-associated, TREM2-associated, and C1q/LAM-like macrophage programs as a practical framework for integrating recurrent TAM states across spatial and treatment contexts. We propose an integrative framework in which TAM state dynamics are associated with, and may contribute to, therapy-refractory phenotypes during (i) ICI therapy through immune exclusion, (ii) oncogene-targeted therapy through macrophage-associated bypass signaling and survival plasticity, particularly in EGFR-TKI resistance, and (iii) post-radiochemotherapy microenvironmental remodeling, with potential implications for residual disease ecosystems that require further clinical validation, particularly with respect to recurrence and relapse. TAM program signatures and spatial organization provide a rationale for investigating biomarker-guided stratification and macrophage-directed combination strategies targeting state-niche axes. Future work should prioritize clinically validated, state- and niche-resolved multimodal biomarkers and prospective translational studies to support rational pairing with ICIs and targeted therapies.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1960604.abstract: To describe serial endoscopic findings in a patient with relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma (MM) and gastric amyloidosis and to summarize 30 published cases, with emphasis on their clinical, endoscopic, and histopathologic features and common diagnostic challenges. This study comprised a case report and an individual-patient pooled analysis of published cases. We reviewed the clinical course and serial endoscopic assessments of the index patient and searched PubMed, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, and Embase from inception through June 1, 2026. Reports of MM-associated gastric amyloidosis with extractable clinical information were included. Demographic characteristics, symptoms, sites of involvement, endoscopic findings, diagnostic methods, clonal characteristics, treatment, and outcomes were analyzed descriptively. During myeloma relapse, the index patient developed refractory nausea and vomiting. Routine histopathologic examination of a biopsy from a proliferative lesion in the gastric fundus showed a fundic gland polyp, while Congo red staining was weakly positive. Symptoms improved substantially after anti-multiple myeloma treatment was resumed, and repeat endoscopy after two cycles of anti-multiple myeloma treatment showed fewer and smaller polypoid elevations. As the disease subsequently progressed, nausea and vomiting recurred intermittently and the polypoid elevations gradually increased, raising the possibility that the gastric manifestations tracked plasma-cell clonal activity. Thirty previously published patients were included. Bleeding-related manifestations were most common (20/30, 66.7%), followed by nausea and vomiting (10/30, 33.3%). The antrum was the most frequently involved site (16/26, 61.5%). Endoscopic findings were available for 28 patients; nodules, polyps, masses, or other nonhematomatous elevated lesions predominated (16/28, 57.1%). Among 25 patients with a clear diagnostic sequence, 14/25 (56.0%) were diagnosed with MM or smoldering multiple myeloma after gastrointestinal amyloid deposition was identified, whereas 11/25 (44.0%) developed gastric involvement in the setting of previously diagnosed MM. MM-associated gastric amyloidosis lacks specific symptoms and endoscopic features. Bleeding, refractory vomiting or obstruction, and tumor-like lesions are important presentations. In patients with MM who have unexplained persistent gastrointestinal symptoms, or discordance among the clinical presentation, endoscopic phenotype, and histopathologic findings, multiple adequate biopsies should be obtained, with deeper sampling when necessary, followed by Congo red staining, confirmation under polarized light, and amyloid protein typing.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1961159.abstract: Background Perineural invasion (PNI) is an aggressive biological feature of colorectal cancer (CRC) driven by active crosstalk between tumor cells, Schwann cells, and the neural microenvironment. Although PNI is associated with recurrence, distant metastasis, and chemoresistance, its pathologic diagnosis is constrained by sampling limitations and inter-observer variability, and direct patient-level evidence linking PNI to the cellular sensitivity of specific cytotoxic agents such as capecitabine is lacking. Methods We performed a retrospective dual-cohort study of 724 patients with histologically confirmed colorectal adenocarcinoma who underwent R0 resection between January 2024 and August 2025 at a tertiary cancer center in China. Cohort A (n = 430) was used to develop and validate a clinicopathologic nomogram for PNI through LASSO regression, multivariable logistic modeling, bootstrap-corrected internal validation, and internal hold-out validation. Discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility were assessed by area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), mean absolute error (MAE), Hosmer–Lemeshow test, and decision curve analysis. The association between PNI and distant metastasis was examined in the full cohort by multivariable logistic regression. Cohort B (n = 390) underwent ATP-based in vitro tumor chemosensitivity assays on patient-derived tumor cells; the association between PNI status and capecitabine sensitivity was evaluated by ordinal logistic regression with inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) and propensity score matching (PSM). Results The six-factor nomogram (T stage, N stage, lymphovascular invasion, tumor budding, KRAS, Ki-67) achieved AUCs of 0.778, 0.741, and 0.803 in the development subset, internal hold-out validation subset and full cohort, respectively, with MAE of 0.023 and Hosmer–Lemeshow P = 0.56. PNI was independently associated with distant metastasis.Patient-derived tumor cells from PNI-positive tumors exhibited markedly reduced in vitro capecitabine sensitivity, consistent across IPTW (multivariable OR = 0.62, 95% CI 0.44–0.88, P = 0.007) and PSM (multivariable OR = 0.34, 95% CI 0.15–0.77, P = 0.009) analyses. Conclusions PNI-positive CRC harbors a reduced in vitro capecitabine sensitivity and an elevated metastatic propensity. The proposed six-factor nomogram offers a practical postoperative tool for PNI risk stratification, while the convergent clinical and in vitro evidence may inform hypothesis-generating individualized strategies pending prospective validation of fluoropyrimidine-based adjuvant therapy in PNI-positive patients.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1961666.abstract: Estrogen receptor-negative/progesterone receptor-positive/human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-negative (ER-/PR+/HER2-)breast cancer is a rare, controversial type that makes up about 0. 3% of all breast cancer cases and does not follow the traditional ER→PR regulatory hierarchy. This review synthesizes the available evidence on the diagnostic evaluation, clinicopathological characteristics, molecular mechanisms, prognosis, and treatment of ER-/PR+/HER2-(ER-/PR+) breast cancer. Although there are false-negative ER staining results and pre-analytical/analytical factors, a number of clinical and transcriptomic data support the existence of a reproducible ER-/PR+subgroup with molecular heterogeneity. These tumors often have a high histological grade, elevated Ki-67 expression, TP53 alterations, and basal-like features, and are closer to triple-negative breast cancer than luminal disease. Potential drivers include ER-independent non-canonical PR activation, epigenetic dysregulation, kinase-mediated receptor phosphorylation, membrane-associated progesterone signaling and receptor network reprogramming. Direct subtype-specific evidence remains limited, and the effectiveness of conventional endocrine therapy is unknown. Current guidelines classify these tumors as hormone receptor-positive/HER2-negative, obscuring clinically relevant heterogeneity. Standardized repeat testing and multi-omic characterization are thus required. Future studies should prioritize prospective multicenter cohorts with paired pre-treatment and post-treatment receptor testing, spatial or single-cell characterization, biomarker-guided stratification and adaptive clinical trials. A PR-oriented precision-medicine framework may improve diagnostic classification and help identify therapeutic vulnerabilities in biologically distinct patient subsets. In addition, this rare phenotype may serve as a useful model for investigating lineage plasticity and endocrine resistance.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1962784.abstract: Ginsenoside Rb2 has demonstrated antitumor activity in multiple malignancies, yet its role in cervical cancer and the underlying mechanism remain unclear. This study investigated the effects of Rb2 on cervical cancer progression and explored whether metabolic reprogramming contributes to PD-L1 regulation. Cell proliferation, migration, invasion, glycolytic activity, lactate production, histone lactylation, and PD-L1 expression were evaluated in cervical cancer cells using CCK-8, EdU, colony formation, wound-healing, Transwell, Seahorse analysis, RT-qPCR, western blotting, flow cytometry, and ChIP-qPCR. LDHA regulation was examined by protein and mRNA stability assays, pharmacological inhibition, lysosome immunoprecipitation, gain- and loss-of-function studies, co-immunoprecipitation, molecular docking, and biotinylated Rb2 pull-down assays. T-cell function was assessed by Jurkat T-cell-tumor cell co-culture and IL-2 ELISA. Xenograft models and clinical samples were used for validation. Rb2 significantly inhibited cervical cancer cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and xenograft tumor growth, reducing HeLa and SiHa cell viability by approximately 23.4% and 25.7%, respectively. Rb2 selectively downregulated PD-L1 and suppressed glycolysis and lactate production, with reduced H3K18la/H4K12la lactylation at the PD-L1 promoter. LDHA was the primary glycolytic enzyme reduced by Rb2, without changes in its mRNA. Rb2 decreased LDHA protein stability and promoted its autophagy-lysosome-dependent degradation, with p62 required and the p62-LDHA interaction enhanced by Rb2. Rb2-pretreated tumor cells restored IL-2 production by co-cultured Jurkat T cells, whereas LDHA overexpression reversed this effect. LDHA overexpression partially rescued Rb2's effects, and LDHA correlated positively with PD-L1 in cervical cancer tissues. Rb2 suppresses cervical cancer progression by promoting p62-dependent autophagic degradation of LDHA, thereby inhibiting glycolysis-associated H3K18la and PD-L1 transcription. These findings reveal a p62/LDHA/H3K18la/PD-L1 signaling axis through which Rb2 exerts its antitumor effects.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1963032.abstract: To determine whether heterogeneous genomic alterations detected by clinical tumor panels converge on a reproducible pathway-level difference between hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and cholangiocarcinoma (CCA), and to examine its transcriptional output, cellular localization, and tumor-stromal coexpression context in public multi-omics cohorts. The institutional cohort comprised 52 patients who underwent tumor tissue genomic testing, including 28 with HCC and 24 in a CCA working cohort whose intrahepatic location was not uniformly documented. Ten canonical oncogenic pathways were compared using panel-aware evaluable denominators, and the selected pathway was tested in independent Memorial Sloan Kettering (MSK) cohorts. Matched genomic and transcriptomic data from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) were used to evaluate downstream pathway activity. GSE151530 and GSE189903 were analyzed by patient-level pseudobulk to localize the transcriptional difference, followed by CellChatDB-guided ligand-receptor coexpression analysis. Receptor tyrosine kinase-RAS (RTK-RAS) showed the strongest cancer-type difference in the institutional cohort: alterations were detected in 4/21 evaluable HCC cases and 8/11 evaluable CCA cases (odds ratio [OR] = 9.44; 95% CI, 1.87-47.70; P = 0.00601; Benjamini-Hochberg-adjusted q = 0.0601), with concordant directions across sensitivity analyses. In MSK, integrated RTK-RAS alterations occurred in 240/412 intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA) cases (58.3%) and 107/289 HCC cases (37.0%; OR = 2.37; 95% CI, 1.74-3.22; P = 3.12 × 10-8). In TCGA, RTK-RAS status was associated with higher mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) activity in the pooled cancer-type-adjusted model (β = 0.240; 95% CI, 0.051-0.428; P = 0.0129), whereas the within-iCCA estimate was positive but imprecise. Patient-level single-cell meta-analysis localized the higher iCCA MAPK activity predominantly to malignant cells (pooled effect = 1.455; 95% CI, 0.658-2.252; P = 3.46 × 10-4; q = 0.00208). Platelet-derived growth factor (PDGF)-PDGFRA and insulin-like growth factor (IGF)-IGF1R coexpression patterns accompanied this malignant-cell phenotype. Panel-aware integration of clinical genomic testing and public multi-omics data supports a higher burden of heterogeneous RTK-RAS alterations in CCA/iCCA than in HCC and links this difference to a malignant-cell MAPK transcriptional phenotype. The pathway-level framework complements, rather than replaces, established alteration-specific interpretation and generates tumor-stromal coexpression hypotheses for further spatial and functional testing.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1963925.abstract: The transportability of models for postoperative high-volume cervical nodal disease in papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) and the incremental predictive value of molecular variables remain uncertain. We developed models in the public Deyang cohort (521 patients; 90 events) and performed geographic external validation in the independent Liaocheng cohort (193 patients; 73 events). The outcome was >5 pathologically confirmed metastatic cervical lymph nodes. Five algorithms were compared using repeated stratified nested cross-validation with a prespecified 10-variable postoperative feature set. Ridge logistic regression (C = 0.1) was selected and applied without refitting. Paired comparisons of 8-variable clinicopathological and 10-variable clinicopathological-molecular models assessed the incremental value of high-risk co-mutation status and mutation count in both cohorts. Internal validation yielded an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.795 (95% CI, 0.745-0.842), average precision (AP) of 0.497 (0.406-0.598), and Brier score of 0.115 (0.098-0.134). External AUROC was 0.752 (0.678-0.821), AP 0.601 (0.498-0.728), and Brier score 0.217 (0.180-0.254). Observed and mean predicted risks were 37.8% and 23.9%, respectively; the observed-to-expected ratio was 1.582 (1.319-1.860) and the weak-calibration slope was 0.831 (0.542-1.191). At the prespecified threshold of 0.158, sensitivity was 0.795 and specificity 0.600. Net benefit was 0.254 for the model and 0.261 for classifying all patients as high risk (difference, -0.008; 95% CI, -0.051 to 0.033). External paired differences after adding molecular variables were +0.002 for AUROC (-0.005 to 0.010), -0.002 for AP (-0.016 to 0.010), -0.001 for Brier score (-0.002 to 0.000), and +0.009 for net benefit (-0.003 to 0.026). The model retained moderate discrimination across centers but underestimated absolute risk and did not demonstrate a net benefit advantage over classifying all patients as high risk at the prespecified threshold. High-risk co-mutation status and mutation count showed no clear incremental predictive value. Further validation with standardized lymph-node assessment and patient outcomes is required before clinical application.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1964406.abstract: Accurate voxel-level segmentation of pulmonary nodules on chest CT is needed for diameter and volume measurement, growth tracking, and quantitative assessment in lung cancer screening. The task remains difficult: nodules vary in attenuation, size, and contact with vessels or pleura, and clinically relevant morphology often lies in a thin, ambiguous margin. Existing systems commonly trade contour fidelity for speed-large prompt-driven foundation models can be accurate but slow, whereas compact CNN or SSM decoders are efficient yet tend to smooth spiculated and ground-glass borders. We propose HSV-Net (Hybrid State-space-Vision Network), a dual-stream 3D network that is prompt-free after nodule localization: an SSM3D stream provides whole-patch context with linear-complexity state-space blocks, and an OrthoLoRA stream adapts frozen DINOv2 features on axial, coronal, and sagittal slices. A Hybrid Gated Mixer (HGM) fuses the two streams before FPN decoding, and Progressive Contour Learning (PCL) supervises overlap, signed-distance-field geometry, and uncertainty-weighted contour refinement. On a 10-patient QIN Lung CT/QIN-LungCT-Seg development subset (n = 12 tumors; nested patient-level 5-fold CV), HSV-Net obtained the highest mean Dice (90.1% ± 1.0%; 95% CI [88.9, 91.3]) and Boundary F1 (86.3% ± 1.3%) among the compared methods on 128 × 128 × 64 patches, with a latency of 58 ms. A standard full-volume nnU-Net v2 baseline reached 88.6% ± 1.0% Dice on the same QIN folds, still below HSV-Net. On an independent LIDC-IDRI benchmark with expert volumetric consensus masks (186 patients/294 nodules; patient-level 5-fold CV within LIDC, not QIN→LIDC transfer), HSV-Net achieved 87.8% ± 1.1% Dice and 83.6% ± 1.3% Boundary F1, outperforming full-volume nnU-Net (87.1% ± 1.0% Dice). LUNA16 was retained only as a proxy size/localization check with diameter-matched spherical references, not as contour external validation.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1964934.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have improved outcomes in selected patients with metastatic triple-negative breast cancer (mTNBC), particularly those with high programed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression. However, optimal dosing strategies balancing efficacy, toxicity, and cost remain unclear. We report the case of a 34-year-old woman with recurrent mTNBC and high PD-L1 expression (combined positive score, CPS ≥ 60; immunohistochemistry 22C3 pharmDx assay). She achieved durable disease control over 22 months (September 2024 to June 2026) using a combination of gemcitabine maintenance chemotherapy and low-dose intermittent nivolumab (40 mg fixed dose, administered 3-weekly). This de-escalated regimen was adopted due to early treatment toxicity and severe financial constraints. The patient achieved a confirmed partial response by RECIST v1.1 criteria (48% reduction in target lesion size), accompanied by manageable CTCAE Grade 2 hypothyroidism requiring oral levothyroxine replacement. This case illustrates that in biomarker-selected, PD-L1-high mTNBC, combination chemotherapy with low-intensity PD-1 blockade can maintain prolonged antitumor activity. These observations support the working hypothesis of a minimum effective immune dose, warranting prospective evaluation in resource-constrained clinical settings.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1965843.abstract: Hematological malignancies may impair ovarian function even before chemotherapy begins, raising concerns about the effectiveness of oocyte cryopreservation. However, available evidence remains conflicting, partly because of confounding factors and suboptimal study designs. This study investigated whether women with lymphoma show reduced ovarian reserve or impaired ovarian response compared with women without cancer and women with non-hematologic malignancies. We conducted a retrospective analysis of women with Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin lymphomas who underwent oocyte cryopreservation for fertility preservation at our Institution. Each patient was age- and study period-matched to two control groups: one comprising women without cancer undergoing Assisted Reproductive Technologies for infertility, allowing comparison of ovarian reserve markers (Anti-Müllerian Hormone, AMH, and antral follicle count, AFC), and another comprising women with non-hematologic solid tumors to compare ovarian stimulation outcomes. The first comparison included 66 cases and 66 controls without cancer. Median [interquartile range - IQR] serum AMH was 1.97 [1.14-3.23] and 2.94 [2.12-4.60], respectively (p=0.002). However, AFC was similar (18 [12-24] versus 15 [11-21], p=0.16). The second comparison involved 74 cases and 74 non-hematologic cancer controls. Ovarian response was similar between groups, with a median [IQR] number of frozen mature oocytes of 10 [6-15] and 13 [6-16], respectively (p=0.56). Early alterations in follicular function may occur in women with lymphoma. Nevertheless, ovarian response to stimulation appears preserved, supporting the effectiveness of fertility preservation.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1966123.abstract: Recurrent or second primary head and neck cancer (rsHNC) presents a radiotherapeutic challenge due to limited tolerance of previously irradiated tissues. These patients could benefit from dose painting (DP), which focuses on delivering maximal dose to areas of high tumor burden while respecting dose constraints to organs at risk. In this study, we compare clinical outcomes in one group receiving standard reirradiation with a group receiving 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) PET/CT-guided DP. Our standard reirradiation regimen is hyperfractionated radiotherapy (RT) of 1.5 Gy x 40 (60 Gy total dose). For DP, we defined two FDG-based prescription volumes receiving at least 65 Gy and 70 Gy. Thirteen patients receiving standard RT were compared with 10 DP patients. Toxicity was scored using CTCAE v3.0. Disease-related endpoints were locoregional control (LRC), disease-free survival (DFS) and overall survival (OS). The mean composite toxicity score was maximal at the end of RT, with varying patterns across the CTCAE items. No significant difference in toxicity was found between the groups except for dysphagia at 6 months, where the standard RT group had worse scores (p=0.01). No differences were found in LRC and DFS. Two-year OS was 50% in the DP group versus 15% in the standard group (p=0.04), although this may reflect higher comorbidity in the standard group. DP of rsHNC did not increase toxicity compared with standard reirradiation. No evidence of improved disease control was found. However, DP may benefit selected patients, and future studies should focus on identifying these candidates. https://clinicaltrials.gov, identifier NCT02921581.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1966376.abstract: Phyllodes tumors (PTs) can overlap with fibroadenomas clinically and radiologically, and incomplete preoperative characterization can alter surgical planning. We describe three women with borderline or malignant PTs who declined preoperative core needle biopsy; clinical underestimation of malignancy also contributed to proceeding directly to excision. Case 1, a 36-year-old woman with long-standing bilateral masses, had a 63-mm malignant PT with heterologous chondroid and osseous differentiation and osteoclast-like giant cells; two contralateral lesions were fibroadenomas. An involved margin prompted re-excision, with no residual tumor and a final closest histological margin of 20 mm, permitting breast conservation. Case 2, a 68-year-old woman with a 75-mm malignant PT, had mildly prominent ipsilateral axillary nodes on mammography but no abnormal enlargement on axillary ultrasonography. Following malignant PT interpretation on frozen section, wide local excision was converted to total mastectomy; sentinel lymph node biopsy was negative (0/3), and the closest margin was the deep margin at 20 mm. The patient declined postoperative radiotherapy. Case 3, a 53-year-old woman with previous right breast fibroadenoma excision, had a right borderline PT involving the inked margin and contralateral pseudoangiomatous stromal hyperplasia. Re-excision approximately 2 cm beyond the previous surgical margin found no residual tumor. All three patients had satisfactory postoperative wound healing, with no reported complications or recurrence during the reported 6-month follow-up. These cases highlight the need for preoperative tissue diagnosis, attention to discrepant axillary imaging, individualized margin-directed surgery, and long-term surveillance.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1966526.abstract: Aim LGALS3BP (also known as Galectin-3-binding protein, Gal-3BP, or 90 K) is a multifunctional secreted glycoprotein involved in tumor progression and has emerged as a potential biomarker and therapeutic target in several malignancies, including neuroblastoma (NB). Increasing evidence suggests that LGALS3BP contributes to shaping the NB tumor microenvironment (TME), particularly through its enrichment on tumor-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs), where it may regulate tumor-stroma interplay. We investigated whether LGALS3BP contributes to stromal cell modulation in NB and is associated with changes in EV cargo composition. Methods A patient-derived NB cell line naturally lacking LGALS3BP (hNB CTRL) and a matched counterpart ectopically re-expressing LGALS3BP (hNB LGALS3BP) were used. Bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells (BMMSCs) were exposed to NB-derived conditioned media (CM) to assess cytokine secretion and LGALS3BP detection in recipient cells. EV cargo was analyzed by microRNA (miRNA) and proteomic profiling. Selected candidates were validated by qPCR and immunoblotting on NB-derived EVs. Results LGALS3BP-containing CM was associated with an altered BMMSCs secretory profile, while tumor-derived extracellular LGALS3BP was detected in BMMSCs. Seven miRNAs were enriched in LGALS3BP-EVs and reduced in donor cells; four were increased in BMMSCs following EV exposure. Proteomic analysis revealed enrichment of RNA-binding proteins, including SRSF1, in LGALS3BP-EVs. Conclusions LGALS3BP is associated with altered EV cargo composition and BMMSCs secretory responses, potentially contributing to tumor-stroma communication within the NB TME.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1966850.abstract: Introduction Reconstructing the jaw after tumor removal or trauma increasingly relies on custom 3D-printed titanium plates. This customization applies to the implant's shape. It usually does not apply to the internal structure. The width and thickness of the plate are still determined by the designer, based on experience and clinical observation. The critical design parameters of the PSI govern its mechanical performance. Hence, if the design could analyze these parameters and adjust them accordingly, it could help avoid plate fracture. This study introduces a parametric-design approach that closes this gap. Methods The proposed algorithm addresses these challenges by using stress data derived from finite element analysis (FEA) to selectively reinforce only the high-stress regions of a reconstruction plate, rather than uniformly reinforcing the entire plate. The reinforcement is smoothly integrated into the plate’s geometry to prevent abrupt changes in cross-section that could create stress concentrations. The approach was applied to a baseline plate at two regions of elevated stress. Results and discussion Plate A reinforced only the primary zone; this reduced peak stress by 36.0% and strain by 43.8% in that zone, the largest reduction observed across both design variants, and also lowered stress and strain in the second, unmodified zone by 12.7% and 14.3%, respectively. Plate B reinforced both zones; this further reduced stress and strain at the second zone by approximately 30.6% and 33.3%, respectively, and reduced strain at the primary zone by approximately 40.6% relative to baseline. Relative to Plate A, Plate B showed a slightly higher stress at the first zone; this stress remained well below the original baseline value. This work shows that patient-specific implant geometry can be shaped directly by biomechanical feedback. This algorithm offers an efficient computational workflow, enabling implants that are not only anatomically tailored but also mechanically optimized as per given loading conditions.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1967294.abstract: Although pleural tissue debris is occasionally encountered in the drainage systems of patients undergoing catheter or chest tube drainage, its clinical utility has not been reported. Here, we report two cases in which pleural tissue debris retrieved during catheter drainage enabled a definitive diagnosis of malignant pleural effusion (MPE) and molecularly guided treatment decisions. The first case involved a 67-year-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis-associated interstitial lung disease who developed a right pleural effusion suggestive of lung cancer with pleural metastasis. Invasive procedures for tissue acquisition were required; however, biopsy was withheld because of the high risk of pneumothorax and acute exacerbation of the underlying lung disease. Tissue debris was incidentally found in the drainage system. The tissue was adequate for pathological examination and revealed lung squamous cell carcinoma without genomic alterations. Chemoimmunotherapy was initiated without further invasive procedures. The second case involved a 78-year-old woman who presented with a left pleural effusion and a brain lesion, highly suggestive of lung cancer with brain metastasis. She declined invasive diagnostic procedures; however, tissue debris was incidentally collected from the drainage bottle and diagnosed as lung adenocarcinoma. Molecular testing revealed that the tumor harbored an epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) L858R mutation, allowing first-line targeted therapy to be initiated without further invasive testing. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first case report to describe the clinical utility of pleural tissue debris for the diagnosis of MPE and its suitability for molecular profiling. Our report highlights that this previously overlooked byproduct of routine pleural drainage can provide adequate material for histopathological diagnosis, immunohistochemistry, and molecular testing in patients with MPE, particularly those for whom conventional biopsy is contraindicated or declined.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1967814.abstract: This study aimed to provide new insights into systemic treatment for BRAF wild-type metastatic unresectable melanoma, thereby offering a basis for personalized clinical decision-making. PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were searched. Eligible participants were adults with pathologically confirmed BRAF V600 wild-type metastatic unresectable melanoma. Outcomes included progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS). Network meta-analysis (NMA) results were presented as league tables and the surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA) values. In total, 8 randomized controlled trials (RCTs) involving 3,418 patients and 9 systemic treatment strategies were included. One open-label study was rated as having some concerns, while the remaining seven were rated as low risk of bias across all domains and overall. The NMA results showed that, compared to ipilimumab, pembrolizumab, nivolumab, nivolumab + relatlimab, and nivolumab + ipilimumab demonstrated significant advantages in improving OS. Notably, nivolumab + relatlimab ranked first in prolonging OS (SUCRA = 93.94%). In the PFS analysis, this regimen had the highest SUCRA value only within the connected network consisting of dacarbazine, nivolumab, and the combination of nivolumab and relatlimab (SUCRA = 98.86%), although no comparisons or standardized rankings were performed between different PFS networks. The results of OS primary analysis for nivolumab plus relatlimab, as well as its ranking within the corresponding PFS network, are exploratory in nature. They are intended solely to generate research hypotheses and should not be interpreted as evidence of superiority over other treatments or as a basis for changing the current standard of care. Direct head-to-head RCTs are still needed to further clarify the comparative efficacy of the relevant regimens.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1968798.abstract: Medical imaging is crucial for glioma management. Combined with MRI, amino acid PET may improve glioma diagnosis, biopsy targeting, and tumor delineation compared to structural MRI alone. Magnetic resonance spectroscopic imaging (MRSI) complements both structural MRI and PET by detecting metabolites such as N-acetylaspartate (NAA), creatine (Cr), and choline (Cho), which are markers for brain health and tumor malignancy, but is challenged by low spatial resolution. This study evaluates whether upscaled MRSI enhanced by deep learning can improve diagnostic accuracy and serve as a complement or alternative to PET for glioma classification. Ten glioma patients (ages 24-80) were included. Presurgical [18F]-FACBC PET/MRI, including proton 2D MRSI, was acquired for all patients. Thirty-two image-guided biopsies were sampled during surgery from the patients and classified as glioma tissue or non-tumor tissue, and according to IDH1 status. For each biopsy location, tumor-to-background ratio (TBR) and standardized uptake value (SUV) from PET, and tCho/NAA and tCho/tCr ratios from MRSI were calculated. ROC analysis was used to assess the accuracy of [18F]-FACBC PET and upscaled MRSI, and the combinations of these in classifying glioma vs non-tumor tissue and IDH1 status. Among the individual biomarkers evaluated, the tCho/NAA ratio from the deep learning-based model demonstrated the highest apparent AUC for classifying glioma vs. non-tumor tissue (AUC = 0.87, 95% CI: 0.66-1.0), compared with tCho/tCr (AUC = 0.81, 95% CI: 0.54-1:00), SUV (AUC = 0.71, 95% CI: 0.49-0.90), and TBR (AUC = 0.68, 95% CI: 0.48-0.86). Combining TBR with tCho/NAA and/or tCho/tCr improved tissue classification compared to either modality alone, where TBR+tCho/NAA+tCho/tCr showed the best results (AUC = 0.91, 95% CI: 0.71-1.0). MRSI was a poor predictor for IDH1-status (tCho/NAA: AUC = 0.67, 95% CI: 0.44-0.88 and tCho/tCr: AUC = 0.38, 95% CI: 0.17-0.60), while PET was an excellent predictor (SUV: AUC = 0.83, 95% CI: 0.66-0.95 and TBR: AUC = 0.82, 95% CI: 0.65-0.94) and the combination of SUV, tCho/NAA, and tCho/tCr was a best predictor (AUC = 0.96, 95% CI: 0.88-1.0). Combining DL-upscaled MRSI with [18F]-FACBC PET appeared to enhance discrimination between glioma and non-tumor tissue, a finding that warrants validation in larger, prospective studies.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1969514.abstract: Background The clinical efficacy of PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors combined with chemotherapy (± targeted agents) in patients with proficient mismatch repair (pMMR) metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) remains unclear. This study systematically evaluated the efficacy of this regimen. Methods We searched PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and ClinicalTrials.gov for relevant randomized controlled trials (RCTs) published up to May 2026. The primary outcomes were progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS); effect sizes were estimated as hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (95%CIs). Results Six RCTs comprising 1,165 participants were included. The addition of PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors to chemotherapy, with or without anti-VEGF agents, was associated with prolonged PFS (HR = 0.84, 95%CI [0.73, 0.95], P = 0.007) and OS (HR = 0.83, 95%CI [0.73, 0.94], P = 0.004). Subgroup analyses for PFS preliminarily suggested greater benefit in male patients (HR = 0.77, 95%CI [0.64, 0.94], P = 0.010), those with an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 0 (HR = 0.73, 95%CI [0.56, 0.95], P = 0.018), those with liver metastases (HR = 0.82, 95%CI [0.68, 0.98], P = 0.027), those without prior adjuvant therapy (HR = 0.81, 95%CI [0.67, 0.98], P = 0.030), those with a PD-L1 combined positive score (CPS) < 1 (HR = 0.53, 95%CI [0.30, 0.95], P = 0.032), those with synchronous metastases (HR = 0.79, 95%CI [0.63, 0.99], P = 0.037), and those with Kirsten rat sarcoma viral oncogene homolog (KRAS) mutations (HR = 0.49, 95%CI [0.30, 0.80], P=0.005). These subgroup findings are exploratory, and interaction tests were not performed. Conclusions PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors combined with chemotherapy (with or without targeted agents) may improve the prognosis of patients with pMMR mCRC and represent a potential first-line treatment option. Systematic review registration https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/ , identifier CRD420261330186.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1970165.abstract: Glioblastoma represents the most aggressive primary malignant tumor of the central nervous system, characterized by extensive intratumoral heterogeneity, profound immunosuppression, therapeutic resistance, and poor clinical outcomes. Although immunotherapy has revolutionized cancer treatment, its clinical efficacy in GBM remains limited, largely due to the complexity of the tumor ecosystem and the lack of validated predictive biomarkers. Recent advances in single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), spatial transcriptomics, and artificial intelligence (AI)-based computational approaches have provided unprecedented opportunities to decipher tumor heterogeneity and identify clinically actionable biomarkers. This mini-review integrates studies related to scRNA-seq and its combination technology, further elaborating on the tumor plasticity, immune suppression, and metabolic-epigenetic reprogramming mechanisms of GBM. The article systematically summarizes the complete analysis process of integrating single-cell multi-omics data by AI and highlights the application value of AI in validating biomarkers. The above research ideas are expected to overcome clinical resistance problems, optimize patient stratification schemes, and enhance the efficacy of immunotherapy, providing theoretical support for developing highly stable prognostic biomarkers and achieving individualized precise immunotherapy for glioblastoma.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1971063.abstract: Computed tomography (CT)-derived vertebral attenuation has been recognized as an indicator of prognosis for patients undergoing tumor removal, liver transplant, or transcatheter arterial chemoembolization (TACE) therapy, but similar research has not been reported in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) patients treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). This study aims to explore the prognostic value of CT-derived vertebral attenuation in HCC patients treated with ICIs. This retrospective study included HCC patients who received ICI treatment at Wuhan Union Hospital between July 2020 and March 2024. CT-derived vertebral attenuation was assessed by measuring mean Hounsfield unit (HU) values in the center of the first lumbar vertebra (L1) on non-contrast CT scans. Based on the optimal cutoff value derived from X-tile software, patients were classified into the CT-derived L1 attenuation-low group (≤100 HU) and the CT-derived L1 attenuation-high group (>100 HU). A comparison of the baseline characteristics of the two groups was made, followed by a propensity score matching (PSM) analysis to balance the variables. The objective response rate (ORR) and disease control rate (DCR) were calculated for both groups, and Kaplan-Meier survival curves and Cox regression models were used to analyze overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS). The cohort consisted of 357 patients, divided into the L1 attenuation-low group (n = 112) and the L1 attenuation-high group (n = 245). Among all patients, 30.0% (107/357) achieved complete or partial response. After PSM analysis, both groups contained 91 patients. The L1 attenuation-low group had shorter OS (hazard ratio [HR], 1.73; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.15-2.60; P = 0.008) and PFS (HR, 1.47; 95% CI, 1.04-2.08; P = 0.030) than the L1 attenuation-high group. CT-derived L1 attenuation can stratify survival risk for HCC patients undergoing ICI treatment.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1971354.abstract: Primary adrenal malignant rhabdoid tumor (MRT) is a rare, highly aggressive neoplasm lacking specific clinical manifestations and imaging characteristics. This case report delineates the clinical course of a patient with primary adrenal MRT managed at our institution. We provide a comprehensive characterization of the patient's clinical presentation, histopathological and molecular genetic profiles, and the therapeutic strategy employed. Furthermore, we critically examine contemporary evidence regarding its pathogenesis, diagnostic challenges, and therapeutic strategies. A 42-year-old man was initially admitted to the Department of Endocrinology presenting with pyrexia and an adrenal mass. The patient underwent surgical resection of an adrenal mass; definitive histopathological examination and molecular genetic profiling confirmed a diagnosis of primary adrenal MRT. Despite undergoing surgical resection and adjuvant chemotherapy, the patient ultimately succumbed to sudden cardiac death. Primary adrenal MRT represent an exceptionally rare clinical entity. Consequently, clinicians must maintain high suspicion for this diagnosis when evaluating non-functioning adrenal masses, especially those with atypical radiological features or aggressive behavior.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1972153.abstract: Accurate breast tumor segmentation in Dynamic Contrast-Enhanced Magnetic Resonance Imaging (DCE-MRI) is important for reliable diagnosis and treatment planning. However, complex tumor morphology, diverse spatial structures, and indistinct boundaries remain challenging for existing segmentation methods. Convolutional neural network-based methods have limited ability to model long-range dependencies, while Transformer-based methods often introduce substantial computational overhead. Although Mamba-based approaches provide an efficient alternative, conventional scanning strategies may suffer from directional bias and insufficiently capture three-dimensional structural variations. We propose a Boundary-Aware Geometric Mamba Network (BAGMNet) for three-dimensional breast tumor segmentation. BAGMNet establishes a structural representation learning framework that combines geometric modeling, multi-directional state-space propagation, and boundary-aware feature refinement. The Geometric Mamba Encoder constructs complementary spatial representations through multiple geometric transformations, while the Multi-directional Selective State Space module enhances three-dimensional dependency modeling and alleviates the directional bias of conventional Mamba scanning. The Gated State-space Fusion and Adaptive Skip Recalibration modules further integrate local structural details with global contextual information and enhance boundary-related representations during feature propagation. Extensive experiments were conducted on the ISPY1 and Yunnan breast MRI datasets. BAGMNet achieved Dice scores of 70.34% and 79.14%, with average surface distances of 9.79 mm and 8.96 mm on the ISPY1 and Yunnan datasets, respectively. Compared with representative convolutional neural network-, Transformer-, and Mamba-based methods, BAGMNet achieved competitive performance in both regional segmentation accuracy and boundary localization.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1972191.abstract: Pulmonary carcinoid tumorlets are small (< 5 mm) neuroendocrine proliferations that are usually identified incidentally in resected lung tissue. Their coexistence with a spatially separate lung adenocarcinoma is uncommon and may complicate the interpretation of multiple pulmonary nodules. A 71-year-old woman with multiple bilateral pulmonary micronodules that had remained radiologically stable for approximately 2 years was admitted after a newly detected lesion in the apicoposterior segment of the left upper lobe was considered suspicious for lung cancer. She reported occasional chest tightness and intermittent cough with sputum and had never smoked. Bronchoscopy and brush cytology were negative. The patient underwent video-assisted thoracoscopic wedge resection of the left upper lobe lesion. Frozen-section examination showed adenocarcinoma, prompting a left upper lobectomy with systematic lymph-node dissection. A left lower lobe wedge resection was performed to sample representative micronodules. Final pathology showed a 3.0-cm invasive adenocarcinoma (approximately 80% acinar and 20% lepidic patterns), without visceral pleural, definite vascular invasion, or metastasis in 17 sampled lymph nodes (pT1cN0M0, stage IA3). The left lower lobe nodules were reported as pulmonary carcinoid tumorlets and were positive for AE1/AE3, synaptophysin, chromogranin A, CD56, and TTF-1, with a Ki-67 index of approximately 2%. The adenocarcinoma harbored an EGFR exon 21 L858R mutation. She was discharged 1 week after surgery. This case illustrates that pulmonary micronodules accompanying a dominant lung cancer may represent a separate neuroendocrine proliferation rather than intrapulmonary metastases. Diagnosis requires correlation of lesion size, morphology, and immunophenotype. Unsampled contralateral nodules could remain radiologically indeterminate and undergo structured surveillance.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1972315.abstract: Gallbladder polyps (GBPs) and colorectal neoplasia frequently coexist against a background of metabolic dysfunction. This study aimed to investigate the association between the Fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) index and high-risk colorectal adenoma (HRA) in patients with GBPs, and to evaluate the effect modification of gallbladder ultrasound characteristics on this association. This retrospective study included 620 patients with GBPs who underwent colonoscopy at Zhengzhou Central Hospital Affiliated to Zhengzhou University between 2022 and 2025. Patients were classified into no adenoma, non-high-risk adenoma (non-HRA), and HRA groups based on colonoscopic pathology. The Mantel-Haenszel linear trend test was used to assess the dose-response relationship between FIB-4 category and adenoma severity. Multivariable logistic regression was fitted with HRA as the outcome, adjusting for demographic and metabolic covariates. Sensitivity analysis was performed using FIB-4 as a continuous variable (per standard deviation increment). Prespecified subgroup analyses and multiplicative interaction models were conducted, with Wald and likelihood ratio tests (LRTs) evaluating the effect modification of gallbladder wall thickness on the FIB-4-HRA association. The FIB-4 category showed a dose-response relationship with adenoma severity (trend P = 0.0039). The risk of HRA in the high FIB-4 group was elevated in the unadjusted model (OR 5.83, P < 0.001) but attenuated after adjustment (aOR 2.32, P = 0.129). The overall aOR per 1-standard deviation (SD) increase in FIB-4 was 1.09 (P = 0.41). Subgroup analysis revealed that the association between per-1-SD increase in FIB-4 and HRA was present only among patients with gallbladder wall thickening (≥3 mm) (aOR = 6.38, P = 0.003), with no significant association in those with normal wall thickness (aOR = 0.94, P = 0.75). The multiplicative interaction term between FIB-4 and gallbladder wall thickness was significant (Wald P = 0.008, LRT P = 0.001). Subgroup analyses of this study showed that among patients with GBPs and gallbladder wall thickening, elevated FIB-4 was associated with an increased risk of high-risk colorectal adenoma. This association still requires validation in independent external cohorts.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1973812.abstract: Prostate cancer (PCa) is a major malignant tumor threatening men's global health. The plasticizer acetyl tributyl citrate (ATBC), widely used as a substitute for phthalates, is increasingly detected in human tissues; however, its role in PCa cell migration and invasion and the underlying mechanisms remain largely unknown. This study integrated network toxicology, scRNA-seq, transcriptomic analysis, Mendelian randomization (MR), and machine learning. In vitro, LNCaP cell proliferation, migration, and invasion were evaluated after ATBC treatment. ATBC toxicity targets were predicted using public databases. scRNA-seq data were analyzed to identify key cell clusters and candidate genes. Causal relationships between candidate genes and PCa were assessed by MR, and key genes were validated through multiple cohorts and HPA-based immunohistochemistry data. Molecular docking and virtual gene knockout were employed to explore binding affinity and functional impact. In this study, in-vitro experiments were first performed, and it was found that the proliferation, migration and invasion abilities of ATBC-treated LNCaP cells were significantly altered. Subsequently, scRNA-seq data were analyzed to identify key cells (epithelial cells). Next, public databases were used to predict the toxic targets of ATBC, and the results of scRNA-seq and transcriptomic analyses were integrated to screen for potential target genes of ATBC in PCa. Finally, MR and machine-learning techniques were adopted to obtain the key genes (LPCAT1 and PDK1). In addition, molecular docking results for ATBC confirmed favorable binding affinity between the key genes and ATBC. Virtual knockout results also indicated that the key genes played a role in tumor migration and invasion. ATBC exposure may promote PCa migration and invasion by targeting LPCAT1 and PDK1, thereby perturbing cytoskeletal dynamics and metabolic pathways. These findings offer novel mechanistic insights into microplastic-associated PCa progression.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1974237.abstract: Background Muscle strength and muscle mass may decline discordantly in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), but the prognostic relevance of combined strength–mass phenotypes during hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy (HAIC)-based combination therapy is unclear. We evaluated survival and incremental prognostic value according to handgrip strength (HGS) and skeletal muscle index (SMI) phenotypes in patients with unresectable HCC. Methods We performed a secondary analysis of 154 patients from the 1:1 propensity score-matched subset of a previously reported 265-patient cohort receiving HAIC with targeted therapy and immunotherapy. Patients were classified as Normal, SMI-low, HGS-low, or Both-low. Progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) were assessed using Kaplan–Meier and multivariable Cox analyses. Incremental prognostic value for OS was evaluated using Harrell’s concordance index (C-index) and likelihood-ratio tests, with internal validation using bootstrap optimism correction. Results Median follow-up was 22.1 months, as estimated using the reverse Kaplan–Meier method. PFS and OS differed across phenotypes (both log-rank P < 0.001). After multivariable adjustment, HGS-low was associated with shorter PFS (hazard ratio [HR], 2.81; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.71–4.60) and OS (HR, 3.09; 95% CI, 1.87–5.11), and Both-low showed similar associations (PFS: HR, 2.53; 95% CI, 1.40–4.56; OS: HR, 3.72; 95% CI, 2.00–6.92). The 10-patient SMI-low estimates were imprecise for PFS (HR, 0.79; 95% CI, 0.29–2.16) and OS (HR, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.28–2.31). After bootstrap optimism correction, adding low HGS increased the C-index from 0.625 to 0.705, whereas the four-phenotype model yielded 0.701 and did not improve model fit beyond low HGS ( P = 0.798). Conclusion Low HGS, with or without low SMI, was associated with poorer survival. HGS may provide a simple and practical measure for baseline prognostic assessment in unresectable HCC treated with HAIC-based combination therapy.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1974418.abstract: Purpose Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) accounts for more than 75% of renal cell carcinomas and is characterized by high metastatic potential and resistance to therapy. Fibronectin 1 (FN1), a major extracellular matrix glycoprotein, is overexpressed in various cancers and promotes tumor progression; however, its precise molecular mechanisms in RCC remain unclear. Methods We analyzed the expression level of FN1 and its clinical relevance in ccRCC using TCGA database. Subsequently, FN1 was knocked down in ACHN cells, followed by functional assays, RNA sequencing, and Western blot validation. Furthermore, we integrated FN1-interacting proteins from the BioGRID and STRING databases and combined this information with differentially expressed genes to identify key downstream effectors of FN1. Results FN1 was significantly upregulated in ccRCC and strongly associated with lymph node metastasis, distant metastasis, and poor overall survival. FN1 knockdown markedly suppressed invasion of ACHN cells, induced transcriptomic alterations, and downregulated key oncogenes, including CSF2, SOX9, and LAMC2. Pathway analysis revealed significant inhibition of the PI3K–Akt signaling axis. Integrating FN1-interacting proteins with the DEGs identified YWHAZ—a known regulator of the PI3K–Akt pathway—as a critical downstream effector of FN1, whose expression was markedly reduced upon FN1 knockdown. Rescue experiments further showed that YWHAZ overexpression substantially restored FN1 knockdown-impaired invasion but only modestly and non-significantly affected Akt phosphorylation. Conclusion FN1 promotes invasion in RCC cells at least in part through YWHAZ-dependent mechanisms, with partial involvement of PI3K-Akt signaling and additional pathways likely contributing. These findings suggest that the FN1/YWHAZ axis may serve as a candidate prognostic marker and a potential target for future preclinical investigation in RCC.

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1974418.title: FN1 promotes invasion of RCC via YWHAZ-associated signaling with partial involvement of the PI3K-Akt pathway

doi:10.3389/fonc.2026.1975159.abstract: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) is the most common histological subtype of lung cancer, with a dismal prognosis partly attributed to immune evasion mediated by T cell dysfunction within the tumor microenvironment. However, the molecular determinants governing CD8+ cytotoxic T lymphocyte functional competence remain incompletely understood. Chloride intracellular channel 3 (CLIC3) has been implicated in cancer progression, but its role in T cell immunity within the LUAD TME is unknown. We performed single-cell RNA sequencing on tumor tissues from nine LUAD patients spanning three pathological stages (adenocarcinoma in situ [AIS], minimally invasive adenocarcinoma [MIA], and invasive adenocarcinoma [IAC]), integrated with spatial transcriptomics, TCGA-LUAD bulk RNA-seq analysis, and flow cytometric validation in an independent cohort of 32 LUAD patients. Functional module scoring and pseudotime trajectory analysis were applied to characterize CLIC3-associated CTL functional states. CLIC3 was predominantly expressed in CTLs and showed a stage-associated decline from AIS to MIA to IAC. CLIC3+ CTLs exhibited significantly higher module scores for cytotoxicity, cytoskeleton remodeling, interferon signaling, and chemotaxis compared to CLIC3- CTLs. Pseudotime trajectory analysis indicated that CLIC3+ cells were positioned at one end of the inferred transcriptional continuum, corresponding to a functionally active state, while CLIC3- cells were positioned at the other, corresponding to a dysfunctional state, accompanied by a decline in CD247, GZMB, PRF1, and TNF along the trajectory. High CLIC3 expression in TCGA-LUAD was associated with significantly longer overall survival. Flow cytometry showed a stage-associated decrease in CLIC3 expression on CD8+ T cells with increasing tumor invasiveness and poor differentiation. CLIC3 serves as a novel marker of CTL functional competence in LUAD, and its stage-associated downregulation reflects T cell dysfunction during tumor progression. CLIC3 expression in CD8+ T cells may represent a predictive biomarker for immunotherapeutic response and a potential target for restoring T cell function in LUAD.
